Serve with a little more oil poured over and the green onions scattered on top.

name: Bean and avocado tostadas
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Brush the tortillas with a little of the oil and bake 8 minutes, until rigid and blistered.
Fry the beans in the rest of the oil with the cumin and salt for 5 minutes, mashing about half of them.
Spread the beans over the crisp tortillas.
Top with lettuce, avocado, salsa, feta and red onion.
Finish with cilantro and lime, and eat immediately — they soften fast.

name: Breakfast burrito
steps: Fry the pepper in the oil for 5 minutes, add the beans and cumin, and warm through. Tip out.
Melt the butter over a low heat and scramble the eggs slowly, taking them off while still glossy.
Warm the tortillas so they roll without splitting.
Lay the filling in a line down the middle: egg, beans, cheese, avocado, salsa, green onions, cilantro.
Fold the ends in and roll tight, then sear seam-side down in the dry pan for a minute to seal.

name: Fluffy pancakes
steps: Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in one bowl and the milk, eggs and vanilla in another.
Combine them and stop while the batter is still lumpy. Beating it smooth builds gluten and makes flat, chewy pancakes.
Rest the batter 5 minutes while the pan heats to medium-low.
Butter the pan and cook in batches, 2-3 minutes until bubbles break on the surface and stay open, then 1 minute more after flipping.
Serve with the blueberries, maple syrup and yogurt.

name: French toast
steps: Beat the eggs with the milk, cinnamon, vanilla and salt in a wide dish.
Soak the bread for 30 seconds a side — long enough to reach the middle, short enough that it does not fall apart.
Melt the butter over medium-low heat and fry 3 minutes a side, until set through and deep gold.
High heat browns the outside while the custard inside stays raw, so keep it gentle.
Serve with the strawberries, yogurt and maple syrup.

name: Loaded nachos
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Toss the beans with the cumin.
Spread half the chips on a tray, then half the beans, pepper and cheese. Repeat. Layering rather than piling is what stops the bottom half being dry.
Bake 10 minutes, until the cheese has run.
Top with salsa, sour cream, avocado, onion, olives, chili, cilantro and lime.

name: Watermelon and feta salad
steps: Salt the watermelon lightly and leave it 5 minutes, then tip off any liquid that collects.
Layer the watermelon, cucumber and onion on a platter.
Crumble the feta over and add the mint.
Dress with the oil, lime juice and a lot of black pepper. No extra salt — the feta brings it.
Finish with the pumpkin seeds and serve cold.

name: Farro, tomato and herb salad
steps: Simmer the farro in plenty of salted water for 25 minutes, until tender but still chewy in the middle.
Drain and dress it while hot with the oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Cool to room temperature.
Fold through the tomatoes, cucumber, onion, olives and herbs.
Add the feta last so it stays in pieces. Keeps two days.

name: Baked egg muffins
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C and oil a muffin tin thoroughly, corners included.
Beat the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper.
Divide the spinach, pepper, green onions and feta between the cups, then pour the egg over to three quarters full.
Bake 20 minutes, until risen and just set. They sink as they cool — that is normal, not a fault.
Run a knife around each before lifting out. Good cold for three days.

name: Fig, fennel and goat cheese salad
steps: Shave the fennel as thinly as you can and drop it into the lemon juice with a pinch of salt. It softens and stops browning.
Whisk the oil, vinegar and honey together.
Spread the arugula on a platter with the drained fennel.
Arrange the figs over, crumble on the goat cheese, and scatter the walnuts.
Spoon over the dressing and grind on plenty of pepper.

name: Pomegranate and herb couscous
steps: Pour the boiling stock over the couscous, cover, and leave 5 minutes. Fork it through with half the oil and cool.
Whisk the rest of the oil with the lemon juice, cumin, salt and pepper.
Fold the herbs, green onions and dressing through the couscous.
Add the pomegranate seeds, almonds and feta and turn over gently.

name: Tomato bruschetta
steps: Salt the diced tomatoes and leave them in a sieve for 10 minutes. The water that drains off is what would otherwise go straight into the toast.
Grill or toast the bread until it has dark edges.
Rub each slice with a cut garlic clove while still hot, then drizzle with oil.
Pile on the tomatoes, add the basil, vinegar and pepper, and eat within a few minutes.

name: Pan con tomate
steps: Toast the bread until crisp right through.
Rub the cut garlic over the rough surface, once or twice only.
Grate the tomato halves on a box grater down to the skin, and discard the skins.
Spoon the pulp over the toast, letting it soak in, then pour over the oil and salt generously.
Four ingredients means each one shows — it is worth using the good oil here.

name: Baba ganoush
steps: Heat the oven to 240°C. Prick the eggplants and roast them whole 30 minutes, until the skins char and they deflate.
Let them cool in a colander so the bitter juices drain away.
Scoop out the flesh and chop it with a knife rather than a blender — blended, it goes pale and gluey.
Beat in the tahini, garlic, lemon juice, cumin and salt, tasting as you go.
Spread in a bowl, pour over the oil, and serve with warm pita and parsley.

name: Muhammara
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 4 minutes and let them cool.
Blitz the peppers, walnuts, breadcrumbs, garlic, lemon juice, cumin, chili flakes, maple syrup and salt to a coarse paste.
Keep it rough. Smooth muhammara loses the point, which is the texture of the nuts.
Loosen with the oil and spread in a shallow bowl.
Scatter the pomegranate seeds over and serve with pita.

name: Warm marinated olives
steps: Warm the oil gently with the garlic, lemon zest, herbs and chili flakes for 3 minutes. Do not let the garlic colour.
Add the olives and warm through for 2 minutes, turning them in the oil.
Take off the heat and leave 10 minutes for the flavours to move into the olives.
Serve warm, with the oil spooned over. They keep a week in the fridge and improve.

name: Deviled eggs
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook 10 minutes, then cool them hard under cold running water.
Older eggs peel far more easily than fresh ones, which is the one time that is an advantage.
Halve them and press the yolks through a sieve into a bowl.
Mash with the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper until smooth, and spoon or pipe back into the whites.
Dust with paprika and scatter with chives.

name: Kale chips
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C. Low and slow, not hot — a fast oven burns the thin edges before the thick ribs dry out.
Wash the kale and dry it completely. Any water left on the leaves steams them soft.
Massage the oil in leaf by leaf, then toss with the nutritional yeast, paprika and salt.
Spread over two trays in a single layer, with nothing overlapping.
Bake 18 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until crisp but still green. Cool on the tray.

name: Stuffed dates
steps: Split each date down one side and lift the stone out.
Press a little goat cheese into each.
Push half a walnut into the cheese.
Arrange on a plate, drizzle with honey, and finish with salt, pepper and mint.

name: Oat and raisin flapjacks
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a tin.
Melt the butter with the maple syrup and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Stir in the oats, raisins, pumpkin seeds, cinnamon and salt until every oat is coated.
Press into the tin firmly — loosely packed flapjacks crumble when cut.
Bake 25 minutes until golden at the edges but still soft in the middle. Score while hot, cool completely in the tin, then cut.

name: Cardamom rice pudding
steps: Bring the rice, milk, sugar and salt to a bare simmer.
Cook 30 minutes on the lowest heat, stirring often and scraping the bottom. It catches easily and the burnt taste goes right through.
Add the raisins for the last 10 minutes.
Stir in the cardamom, cinnamon and vanilla off the heat. It will look loose and thickens a lot as it cools.
Serve warm or cold with the almonds on top.

name: Cinnamon baked apples
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C.
Core the apples but leave the base intact, and score a ring through the skin round the middle so they do not split.
Rub the butter into the oats, walnuts, raisins, cinnamon, salt and half the maple syrup.
Pack the mixture into the apples, sit them in a dish with 100 ml water, and pour the rest of the syrup over.
Bake 30 minutes, basting once, until a knife goes in with no resistance. Serve with yogurt.

name: Berry and banana smoothie
steps: Put the liquid in the blender first and the frozen fruit last — it blends smoothly instead of jamming.
Blend the milk, yogurt, banana, oats, honey and chia seeds until smooth.
Add the frozen berries and blend again.
The oats thicken it as it stands, so drink it fairly promptly or loosen with more milk.

name: Overnight oats
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, chia seeds, maple syrup and cinnamon together in two jars.
Fold in the grated apple and raisins.
Refrigerate overnight, or at least 4 hours.
Add the walnuts in the morning rather than the night before, so they stay crunchy. Loosen with a splash of milk if it has set too firm.

name: Street corn
steps: Get a griddle or heavy pan very hot.
Rub the cobs with the butter and char them, turning, for about 12 minutes, until blackened in patches all round.
Brush each hot cob with mayonnaise — it clings to hot corn and slides off cold.
Roll in the feta, then dust with chili powder and paprika.
Finish with cilantro, salt and a hard squeeze of lime.

name: Chili lime peanuts
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C.
Toss the peanuts with the oil, then the lime zest, chili powder, paprika, sugar and salt.
Spread on a tray and roast 12 minutes, shaking once.
Squeeze the lime juice over while they are still hot and spread them out to dry.
Cool completely before storing, or they go soft in the jar.

name: Cucumber nori rolls
steps: Cook the rice and, while hot, fold through the vinegar, sugar and salt. Spread it out to cool to body temperature.
Lay a nori sheet shiny side down and spread rice over three quarters of it in a thin layer, leaving the far edge bare.
Lay the cucumber, avocado and carrot in a line across the near third.
Roll tightly away from you, dampening the bare edge to seal.
Cut with a wet knife, wiping it between slices, and serve with soy sauce and sesame seeds.

name: Mango lassi
steps: Blend the mango, yogurt, milk, honey and cardamom until completely smooth.
Taste and add the lime juice — a ripe mango needs the acid or the drink is cloying.
Serve very cold, over ice if the mango was not chilled.

name: Spiced poached pears
steps: Bring 700 ml water to a simmer with the sugar, star anise, cinnamon, orange zest and juice.
Lower the pears in and cover with a scrap of baking paper pressed onto the surface, to keep the tops from going brown above the liquid.
Poach 25 minutes at a bare tremble, turning once. A knife should meet no resistance.
Lift the pears out and boil the liquid hard for 5 minutes until syrupy, then stir in the vanilla.
Serve warm or cold with the syrup poured over, the yogurt and the walnuts.

name: Trail mix
steps: Toast the almonds, cashews and pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 5 minutes, shaking often.
Cool them completely before anything else goes in, or the chocolate melts into the lot.
Mix with the raisins, chocolate, cinnamon and salt.
Keeps a month in a sealed jar.

name: Herb frittata with walnuts
steps: Chop the herbs finely and use far more than feels reasonable — this should be green all the way through, held together by egg rather than the other way round.
Beat the eggs with the flour, turmeric, salt and pepper, then fold in the herbs, green onions and walnuts.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a low heat and pour the mixture in.
Cover and cook 20 minutes on the lowest heat, until set at the edges and only just wobbling in the centre. Rushing it browns the herbs and turns them bitter.
Finish under the grill for 3 minutes, rest, and cut into wedges. Serve with yogurt and warm pita.

name: Lentil rice with dates and raisins
steps: Steep the saffron in 3 tablespoons of hot water while everything else cooks.
Fry the onions in half the butter for 12 minutes, until deep brown. Lift half out for the top.
Simmer the lentils in plenty of salted water for 18 minutes, until tender but whole, and drain.

Boil the rice in heavily salted water for 7 minutes only, then drain. Layer it with the lentils, dates, raisins, cinnamon and cumin in the pan, dot with the rest of the butter, and pour the saffron water over.
Cover with a tea towel under the lid and steam 15 minutes on the lowest heat. Serve with the reserved onions, pistachios and yogurt.

name: Cheese and egg bread
steps: Heat the oven as high as it goes with a tray inside.
Divide each dough ball in two and stretch each piece into an oval on a floured surface.
Mix the mozzarella and feta and heap it down the middle, then roll the long edges in over the filling and pinch the ends together to make a boat.
Bake on the hot tray 15 minutes, until the crust is set and the cheese is bubbling.
Pull them out, make a dip in the cheese, slide an egg into each and return for 4 minutes until the white is just set. Dot with butter and serve with the greens.

name: Georgian walnut bean stew
steps: Soften the onions in the oil for 10 minutes.
Blitz or pound the walnuts with the garlic, half the cilantro, the coriander and paprika into a coarse paste with a splash of the stock.
Add the beans and the rest of the stock to the onions and simmer 10 minutes, crushing about a third of them.
Stir in the walnut paste and cook 5 minutes more. It should be thick enough to hold a spoon upright.
Finish with the vinegar, the rest of the cilantro and plenty of pepper, and serve with cornbread.

name: Sri Lankan coconut dhal
steps: Simmer the lentils with the turmeric and 700 ml water for 15 minutes, until soft.
Add the coconut milk and salt and cook 5 minutes more. Keep it loose — it thickens off the heat.
In a small pan, heat the oil and pop the mustard and fennel seeds, then add the onion and fry 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, chili flakes and cinnamon for a minute, then tip the whole panful into the dhal.
Finish with lime juice and cilantro and serve with roti.

name: Kottu roti
steps: Shred the roti into short ribbons with a knife — this is a dish built out of chopping, and the pieces want to stay distinct.
Get a wide pan very hot with the oil. Fry the onion, leek and carrot for 5 minutes, then the cabbage for 3.
Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and chili flakes for a minute.
Push everything aside, scramble the eggs in the gap, then combine.
Add the roti and soy sauce and toss hard for 2 minutes. Finish with cilantro and lime.

name: Okra do pyaza
steps: Dry the okra completely and cut it only when dry. Wet okra goes slimy the moment it hits the pan.
Fry it in half the oil over high heat for 8 minutes without stirring much, until the edges brown. Lift out.
Soften the onions in the rest of the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and ground spices.
Add the red onion and salt and cook 6 minutes, until the onion is soft at the edges but still has bite. Finish with the lemon juice.
Fold the okra back in for 2 minutes only, finish with garam masala and cilantro, and serve with roti.

name: Yogurt and chickpea flour curry
steps: Start the rice.
Whisk the yogurt, chickpea flour, turmeric, salt and 900 ml water until completely lump-free.
Bring it to a simmer over medium heat, stirring constantly until it thickens. Stop stirring before it boils and the yogurt splits — steady movement is the whole technique.
Simmer gently 20 minutes, stirring often, until it coats a spoon and no longer tastes of raw flour.
Heat the oil in a small pan, pop the mustard seeds, add the cumin, chili flakes, garlic and ginger, and pour it over. Serve on rice with cilantro.

name: Vegetable pulao
steps: Soak the rinsed rice in cold water for 10 minutes while you prepare everything else, then drain it well.
Fry the onion in the butter for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, whole and ground spices for a minute.
Add the carrot and beans and stir for 2 minutes, then the drained rice, turning until every grain is glossed.
Pour in the stock and salt, bring to the boil, cover, and cook on the lowest heat 12 minutes. Add the peas for the last 3.
Rest 5 minutes off the heat before lifting the lid, then fork through. Serve with cashews, yogurt and cilantro.

name: Pav bhaji
steps: Boil the potatoes, cauliflower and peas together until very soft, about 15 minutes, then drain.
Fry the onion in half the butter for 8 minutes, add the garlic, ginger, peppers and all the spices, then the roasted peppers and salt. Cook 8 minutes, mashing them down.
Tip in the drained vegetables and mash the whole lot in the pan until it is a rough, spoonable mixture.
Cook 5 minutes more, adding water if it stiffens, and taste hard for salt and chili.
Split the buns and toast them cut side down in the rest of the butter. Serve with lemon, raw red onion and cilantro.

name: Vegetable momos
steps: Salt the chopped cabbage and leave it 10 minutes, then squeeze it dry. A wet filling steams the wrappers apart from the inside.
Mix it with the carrot, green onions, tofu, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, soy sauce and salt.
Put a spoonful in each wrapper, wet the rim, and pleat or simply fold into a half moon and press firmly.
Steam in a lined steamer 12 minutes, in batches, not touching.
For the sauce, char the roasted peppers in a dry pan until they blister, then blitz with the chili flakes, cilantro and salt. Serve hot.

name: Japchae
steps: Boil the noodles 6 minutes, drain, rinse, and cut through them a few times with scissors so they are manageable.
Mix the soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar and garlic into a dressing.
Cook each vegetable separately in a little vegetable oil — onion and pepper 3 minutes, mushrooms 5, carrot 2, spinach until just wilted and then squeezed dry.
Beat and fry the eggs as a thin omelette, roll it and slice into ribbons.
Toss everything with the noodles and dressing while still warm, and finish with sesame seeds and green onions.

name: Green onion pancakes
steps: Whisk the flour, cornstarch, eggs, salt and 300 ml ice-cold water into a thin batter. Cold water and cornstarch are what make the edges crisp rather than bready.
Fold in the green onions, carrot and zucchini.
Heat a third of the oil in a wide pan until it shimmers and pour in a quarter of the batter, spreading it thin.
Cook 4 minutes until the underside is lacy and brown, flip, press flat, and give it 3 more. Repeat.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, chili flakes and sesame seeds for dipping, and cut the pancakes into squares.

name: Soybean paste stew
steps: Start the rice.
Bring the stock to a simmer with the potato and onion and cook 8 minutes.
Whisk the miso and gochujang with a ladle of the hot broth in a cup, then stir it back in. Added straight to the pot it sits in lumps.
Add the mushrooms, zucchini and chili flakes and simmer 6 minutes.
Slide the tofu in for the last 3 minutes, add the garlic, and finish with green onions. Serve with rice.

name: Eggplant in garlic sauce
steps: Start the rice.
Toss the eggplant batons in 2 tablespoons of the cornstarch.
Fry them in the oil over high heat, in two batches, until browned and collapsing, about 6 minutes each. Lift out.
Fry the garlic, ginger and white parts of the green onions for 30 seconds, then add the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, gochujang and stock.
Stir the remaining cornstarch into a splash of cold water, add, and simmer until glossy. Return the eggplant, toss, and finish with sesame oil and green onion tops.

name: Tomato and egg stir-fry
steps: Start the rice.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt. Get the pan hot with half the oil, pour them in, and pull them into big soft curds. Take them out while still glossy — they cook again later.
Add the rest of the oil and the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes, pressing them so they release their juice into a sauce.
Add the garlic, sugar, soy sauce and salt. The sugar is not optional; it is what stops the tomatoes tasting sharp.
Return the eggs, fold through for thirty seconds, and finish with sesame oil, green onions and pepper.

name: Vegetable lo mein
steps: Cook the noodles just short of done and drain — they finish in the pan.
Mix the soy sauce, hoisin, vinegar, cornstarch and 80 ml water.
Get the pan very hot with the oil. Fry the mushrooms 4 minutes, then the carrot and cabbage 3, then the snap peas, garlic and ginger for 1.
Add the noodles and the sauce and toss until everything is coated and the sauce clings.
Finish with sesame oil and green onions.

name: Tofu katsu curry
steps: Start the rice. Press the tofu slabs dry under something heavy.
Fry the onion and carrot in the butter for 10 minutes, add the curry powder and flour left over from dredging, then the stock, soy sauce and mirin. Simmer 15 minutes and blend if you want it smooth.
Dredge the tofu in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing the crumbs on firmly.
Shallow-fry in the oil, 3 minutes a side, until deep gold. Drain on paper and salt straight away.
Slice and serve over rice with the sauce poured alongside and the raw cabbage on the side.

name: Yaki udon
steps: Loosen the udon in hot water and drain.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, hoisin and vinegar.
Get the pan smoking with the oil. Fry the mushrooms 3 minutes, then the cabbage and carrot 3 more, leaving them alone between stirs so they catch.
Add the udon and sauce and toss hard for 2 minutes, letting the noodles sit against the pan to colour.
Fry the eggs separately and serve on top with sesame oil, green onions and nori.

name: Mushroom and egg rice bowl
steps: Cook the rice.
Simmer the stock, soy sauce, mirin and sugar with the onion in a wide shallow pan for 5 minutes.
Add both mushrooms and cook 6 minutes until they give up their liquid.
Pour the loosely beaten eggs over in a spiral and cover. Do not stir. Two minutes gives you set edges and a barely-set middle, which is the point.
Slide over the rice and finish with green onions and nori.

name: Pad see ew
steps: Soak the noodles until pliable and drain. Mix the soy sauce, hoisin, vinegar and sugar.
Brown the tofu in half the oil over the highest heat you can manage and set aside.
Add the rest of the oil, the broccoli and a splash of water, and cover for 2 minutes.
Push aside, scramble the eggs in the gap, then add the garlic, noodles and sauce.
Toss as little as possible and let the noodles sit against the pan between turns — the charred edges are the dish. Finish with tofu, pepper and lime.

name: Tom kha mushroom soup
steps: Start the rice.
Simmer the stock with the ginger for 8 minutes to draw the flavour out, then add the coconut milk.
Stir in the curry paste, soy sauce and sugar and bring to a bare simmer. Do not let it boil hard or the coconut milk splits.
Add the mushrooms and pepper and cook 8 minutes.
Take it off the heat before adding the lime juice — boiled lime turns bitter. Finish with chili and cilantro and serve with rice.

name: Massaman potato curry
steps: Start the rice.
Fry the curry paste in the oil for 2 minutes, then add half the coconut milk and cook until the oil splits out and it smells rich, about 5 minutes.
Add the rest of the coconut milk, the potatoes, carrots, onion, cinnamon and cardamom, and simmer 25 minutes.
Season with the tamarind, soy sauce and sugar — massaman wants all three of sour, salty and sweet, and it tastes flat if one is missing.
Stir in the peanuts and finish with lime and cilantro.

name: Tofu adobo
steps: Start the rice.
Brown the tofu hard in the oil on several sides and lift out.
Fry the garlic for a minute, then add the soy sauce, vinegar, bay, pepper, sugar and 200 ml water.
Simmer 5 minutes without stirring before you taste it — raw vinegar is harsh and needs the time to mellow.
Return the tofu and simmer 12 minutes until the sauce is syrupy. Steam the bok choy over the top for the last 4 minutes and serve on rice.

name: Mee goreng
steps: Cook the noodles just short of done and drain.
Mix the sriracha, soy sauce, hoisin and maple syrup into a thick sauce.
Brown the tofu in half the oil over high heat and set aside.
Fry the garlic and cabbage 3 minutes, push aside and scramble the eggs, then add the noodles and sauce.
Toss hard for 2 minutes, add the sprouts and tofu for thirty seconds, and finish with lime, cucumber and green onions.

name: Jollof rice
steps: Blend the roasted peppers, fresh peppers, one onion and the chili to a smooth purée.
Fry the other onion in 3 tablespoons of the oil for 8 minutes, add the spices, and cook 3 minutes.
Pour in the purée and cook it hard for 12 minutes, until it darkens and thickens. That reduction is the whole dish — stop early and you have pepper soup with rice in it.
Stir in the rice and stock, cover tightly, and cook on the lowest heat 20 minutes without lifting the lid. Add the peas for the last 3.
Fry the plantain slices in the rest of the oil until caramelised, and serve alongside.

name: Atkilt wat
steps: Fry the onions in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes, until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric, cumin and coriander and cook 2 minutes.
Add the potato and carrot with 150 ml water, cover, and cook 12 minutes.
Add the cabbage and collards, season, cover again, and cook 12 minutes more. It steams in its own liquid rather than frying, so keep the lid on.
Serve on injera, with the vegetables still holding their shape.

name: Shiro
steps: Cook the onions in the oil over medium heat for 12 minutes, until soft and beginning to colour.
Add the garlic, ginger, paprika, chili powder and cardamom and cook 2 minutes.
Whisk the chickpea flour into the cold stock separately until smooth, then pour it in slowly, stirring.
Simmer 12 minutes, stirring often. It thickens fast and catches easily, and it must lose its raw-flour taste.
Season and serve on injera with the green onions and cilantro.

name: Chakalaka with beans
steps: Fry the onion and peppers in the oil over high heat for 8 minutes, so they take some colour.
Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder, paprika and chili flakes for a minute.
Stir in the grated carrot and cook 3 minutes — grated rather than diced is what gives chakalaka its texture.
Add the roasted peppers, stock and beans, season, and simmer 10 minutes.
Serve warm or at room temperature with cornbread and cilantro.

name: Black bean feijoada
steps: Start the rice.
Brown the mushrooms hard in half the oil, then add the onion and carrot for 8 minutes and the garlic, paprika, cumin and bay for a minute.
Add the beans and stock, season, and simmer 20 minutes, mashing some against the pot until it is thick and dark.
Fry the shredded collards in the rest of the oil over high heat for 3 minutes only, so they stay bright.
Serve the beans over rice with the greens and the orange segments — the fruit cuts the richness and is not a garnish.

name: Potatoes in chilli cheese sauce
steps: Boil the potatoes whole in salted water for 22 minutes, then peel and slice them thickly.
Boil the eggs 9 minutes, cool and halve.
Fry the onion, garlic and chilies in the oil for 8 minutes.
Blend them with the cheese, milk and crackers until completely smooth. The crackers are the thickener — add more if it will not coat a spoon.
Season, and pour over the warm potatoes on a bed of lettuce with the eggs and olives.

name: Sopa de fideo
steps: Fry the broken pasta in the oil over medium heat, stirring, for 5 minutes until it is a deep toasted brown. This is the whole flavour of the soup and it is easy to under-do.
Blend the roasted peppers, onion, garlic and cumin smooth and pour it in — stand back, it spits.
Cook 5 minutes until it darkens, then add the stock and salt.
Simmer 10 minutes until the pasta is soft. It should stay soupy; add stock if it thickens.
Serve with avocado, queso fresco, lime and cilantro.

name: Rajas con crema
steps: Char the peppers in a dry hot pan until blackened in patches, then slice.
Fry the onion in the oil over medium-high heat for 10 minutes, until well browned at the edges.
Add the garlic, cumin, oregano, corn and peppers and cook 4 minutes.
Stir in the cream and cheese off the boil and cook gently until it coats, 3 minutes. Boiling will split it.
Season, add the sour cream, and serve in warm tortillas with lime and cilantro.

name: Huevos rancheros
steps: Fry the onion and chili in half the oil for 6 minutes, add the garlic and cumin, then the roasted peppers blended with the stock, and the salt. Simmer 12 minutes.
Warm the beans through in a second pan with a splash of water, mashing about half.
Crisp the tortillas one at a time in the rest of the oil, 30 seconds a side, and drain.
Fry the eggs so the whites are set and the edges lacy.
Stack two tortillas per plate with beans, then the egg, then the sauce spooned round it. Top with queso fresco, avocado, cilantro and lime.

name: Vegetable jambalaya
steps: Fry the onion, pepper and celery in the oil for 10 minutes — this trio is the base and wants real time.
Add the garlic, paprika, oregano, chili powder and bay for a minute.
Stir in the rice until glossed, then add the roasted peppers, beans, stock and salt.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat 20 minutes without stirring. Stirring rice this way makes it gluey.
Scatter the okra over the top for the last 8 minutes so it steams rather than stews, and finish with green onions.

name: Vegetable gumbo
steps: Make the roux first: whisk the flour into the oil over medium heat and keep whisking for 12 minutes until it is the colour of peanut butter. Do not walk away — it goes from perfect to burnt in seconds.
Add the onion, pepper and celery straight into the hot roux and cook 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, spices and bay, then the stock a ladle at a time, whisking smooth.
Simmer 15 minutes, add the beans and okra, and cook 10 more.
Start the rice while it simmers. Season hard and serve over rice with green onions.

name: Mushroom cheesesteak
steps: Get a wide pan very hot. Brown the mushrooms in the oil in two batches without crowding, 6 minutes each, until they squeak and colour.
Add the butter, onion and pepper and cook 8 minutes, then the garlic and seasoning.
Chop the whole lot roughly in the pan with the edge of a spatula.
Lay the provolone over the top, turn off the heat and cover for 2 minutes to melt it.
Split and toast the rolls, spread with mayonnaise and mustard, and pile the filling in.

name: Three sisters stew
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and spices for a minute.
Add the squash, roasted peppers, beans, stock and salt.
Simmer 22 minutes, until the squash is tender but still in pieces.
Add the corn for the last 5 minutes and crush a ladle of the beans to thicken it.
Finish with lime and cilantro and serve with cornbread.

name: Käsespätzle
steps: Fry the onions in half the butter over medium heat for 18 minutes, until deep brown and sweet. Start these first.
Beat the flour, eggs, milk, nutmeg, salt and pepper into a thick batter and let it stand 10 minutes.
Press it through a colander with large holes into a pan of boiling salted water, in batches. They are done about thirty seconds after they float.
Lift them out and toss with the rest of the butter and both cheeses while still hot, so the cheese melts into strands.
Top with the onions and chives and serve with the dressed greens.

name: Braised cabbage with potato dumplings
steps: Fry the onion in half the butter for 5 minutes, then add the cabbage, apple, vinegar, sugar, caraway, bay, allspice and 150 ml water.
Cover and braise 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. The vinegar goes in at the start, not the end — it keeps the colour and softens the cabbage.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes 20 minutes, drain, and mash them dry.
Work in the flour, egg, nutmeg and salt while warm, and roll into balls. Simmer them 8 minutes in salted water, until they float and hold.
Serve the dumplings with the cabbage, the rest of the butter and parsley.

name: Rösti with fried eggs
steps: Wring the grated potato out in a tea towel, hard. Whatever water you leave in comes out in the pan and steams the rösti instead of crisping it.
Season it and fold through the cheese.
Melt half the butter with the oil in a wide pan and press the potato in as an even cake.
Cook 10 minutes over medium heat without touching it, slide onto a plate, invert, add the rest of the butter and cook 10 minutes more.
Fry the eggs, sit them on top, and serve with sour cream, chives and the dressed greens.

name: Caldo verde
steps: Soften the onion and garlic in half the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the potatoes, stock and salt and simmer 18 minutes until falling apart.
Blend until completely smooth, then stir in the beans and paprika.
Shred the greens as finely as you possibly can — this is the defining detail — and add them for the last 4 minutes only, so they stay bright green and firm.
Finish each bowl with a hard pour of the remaining oil and plenty of pepper. Serve with cornbread.

name: Sauerkraut and cabbage soup
steps: Brown the mushrooms in the oil, then add the onion and carrot for 8 minutes and the caraway for 2.
Add the stock, potatoes, bay and fresh cabbage and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the sauerkraut and beans and cook 12 minutes more. Adding the sauerkraut late keeps its sourness sharp rather than boiled flat.
Season carefully — sauerkraut brings a lot of salt of its own.
Serve with sour cream, dill and rye bread.

name: Yellow pea soup
steps: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the butter for 10 minutes, then add the garlic, thyme and bay.
Add the split peas and stock and bring to the boil, skimming the foam off.
Simmer 35 minutes, until the peas have collapsed. Split peas do not need soaking but they do need the full time.
Stir in the mustard and season hard. Blend half if you want it smoother.
Serve with rye bread and parsley.

name: Seitan reuben
steps: Mix the mayonnaise, mustard, chopped pickles and paprika into a dressing.
Fry the seitan in the oil over high heat for 5 minutes, until browned at the edges.
Squeeze the sauerkraut dry and warm it in the same pan for a minute.
Build each sandwich: dressing, cheese, seitan, sauerkraut, cheese, dressing. Cheese on both sides glues it together.
Butter the outsides and griddle over medium-low heat, pressed, 4 minutes a side until the cheese runs.

name: Cauliflower cheese
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C. Boil the cauliflower 6 minutes, then drain very well and let it steam dry.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, cook 2 minutes, then whisk in the milk gradually until smooth and thickened.
Off the heat, stir in the mustard, nutmeg, most of both cheeses, and season hard.
Fold the beans through the cauliflower in a baking dish — they turn a side dish into supper — and pour the sauce over.
Top with the remaining cheese, the breadcrumbs and thyme and bake 25 minutes until browned and bubbling.

name: Glamorgan sausages
steps: Boil the potatoes for 20 minutes and crush them roughly with a little of the butter.
Sweat the leeks in the rest of the butter for 8 minutes and let them cool — hot leeks will cook the egg.
Mix with the cheese, three quarters of the breadcrumbs, two eggs, the herbs, mustard, salt and pepper, and shape into eight sausages.
Roll them in the remaining crumbs bound with the last beaten egg, and chill 10 minutes if you can.
Fry in the oil, turning, for 8 minutes until golden all round. Serve with the crushed potatoes and dressed greens.

name: Kale stamppot
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water 20 minutes, adding the kale for the last 5.
Meanwhile fry the onions in the oil for 12 minutes until deep brown.
Warm the milk with the butter.
Drain the pot, let it steam dry for a minute, then mash everything together with the hot milk, mustard, nutmeg, salt and pepper. Leave it rough.
Fold the cheese cubes through so they half-melt, and top with the onions.

name: Cheese and filo pie
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C and melt the butter.
Beat the eggs with the yogurt, then fold in both cheeses, the dill, spinach and pepper. It needs no salt.
Brush a sheet of filo with butter, crumple it loosely into the tin, and spoon over some filling. Repeat, layering crumpled sheets and filling, finishing with filo.
Crumpling rather than laying flat is what makes it light — flat layers set into a solid slab.
Brush the top with the last butter and bake 30 minutes until deep gold. Rest 10 minutes and serve with the greens.

name: Stuffed cabbage rolls
steps: Boil the whole cabbage 8 minutes, then peel off twelve outer leaves as they soften and trim the thick ribs flat.
Simmer the lentils 15 minutes and drain. Fry the onion and carrot in the oil for 8 minutes, add the garlic and paprika, then fold in the lentils and raw rice.
Roll a spoonful in each leaf, tucking the sides in, and pack them seam down in a pan.
Blend the roasted peppers smooth, pour them over with the stock, cover, and simmer 25 minutes — the rice finishes cooking inside the rolls.
Serve with sour cream and dill.

name: Saffron risotto
steps: Steep the saffron in a ladle of the hot stock and keep the rest at a bare simmer.
Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes without colouring it.
Stir in the rice for a minute until the grains look translucent at the edges.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, waiting for each to be absorbed. Add the saffron stock halfway through, and the peas near the end. About 20 minutes.
Off the heat beat in the butter and parmesan hard, cover, rest 2 minutes, and serve loose. Finish with lemon zest and pepper.

name: Farinata with tomato salad
steps: Whisk the chickpea flour with 700 ml water and 1 teaspoon of salt until smooth and rest it at least 30 minutes — overnight is better. Skim off any foam.
Heat the oven to 250°C with a heavy pan or tray inside.
Pour half the oil into the hot pan, then the batter to about 5 mm deep, and scatter over the rosemary.
Bake 20 minutes, until set with browned, blistered edges.
Toss the tomatoes, onion, arugula and olives with the rest of the oil and the vinegar, and pile on top. Cut into wedges.

name: Bulgur and walnut bake
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Simmer the lentils 18 minutes and drain.
Pour 350 ml boiling water over the bulgur, cover, and leave 15 minutes.
Fry the onions in half the oil for 10 minutes, then add the spices, walnuts and pomegranate molasses.
Mix everything with the lentils and season well, then press firmly into an oiled dish and score into diamonds.
Pour the rest of the oil over and bake 30 minutes until crusted on top. Serve with yogurt, parsley and pomegranate seeds.

name: Batata harra with chickpeas
steps: Heat the oven to 230°C. Toss the potatoes and chickpeas with two thirds of the oil, the coriander, paprika and salt.
Roast 30 minutes, turning once, until the potatoes are crisp at the corners.
In the last minutes, warm the garlic and chili gently in the rest of the oil until fragrant but not coloured.
Toss the hot potatoes and chickpeas through the garlic oil with the cilantro and lemon juice, off the heat. Added earlier the garlic burns.
Whisk the yogurt with the tahini and serve alongside with warm pita.

name: Chopped salad with tahini
steps: Dice everything to the same small size. The uniformity is the dish — chunks make it an ordinary salad.
Toss the vegetables, parsley and chickpeas with the oil, half the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Whisk the tahini with the rest of the lemon juice and enough cold water to make it pourable.
Spoon the salad over the tahini rather than mixing it in, dust with sumac, and serve with pita.

name: Cucumber and daikon sunomono
steps: Salt the sliced cucumber and daikon and leave them 10 minutes, then squeeze gently and pat dry.
Dissolve the sugar in the vinegar with the soy sauce.
Toss the vegetables through the dressing and chill 15 minutes.
Boil the edamame 4 minutes and cool them, if using.
Serve cold with the sesame oil, sesame seeds and nori scattered over.

name: Wild rice, apple and walnut salad
steps: Simmer the wild rice in plenty of salted water for 35 minutes, until the grains split open but still have bite. Drain well.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, mustard, maple syrup, salt and pepper.
Dress the rice while warm and let it cool.
Fold through the apple, celery, apricots and walnuts.
Add the arugula and blue cheese just before serving.

name: Semolina upma
steps: Toast the semolina in a dry pan over medium heat for 5 minutes, until it smells nutty and turns a shade darker. Skip this and upma turns to paste.
Heat the butter and oil, fry the cashews until golden, then pop the mustard seeds.
Add the onion, chili and ginger for 5 minutes, then the carrot, peas and turmeric.
Pour in 450 ml boiling water with the salt, then rain the semolina in while stirring hard.
Cook 3 minutes until it pulls away from the pan, then cover off the heat for 5. Fluff with lemon juice and cilantro.

name: Moroccan carrot and apricot salad
steps: Toast the cumin and cinnamon in a dry pan for 30 seconds, then stir into the oil with the harissa, lemon juice, honey and salt.
Toss the grated carrot through the dressing and leave it 10 minutes to soften.
Fold in the apricots, chickpeas and herbs.
Scatter the almonds over at the last moment so they stay crisp. Better after an hour.

name: Shopska salad
steps: Char the pepper over a flame or under the grill until blackened, then peel and dice it.
Toss the cucumber, pepper, radish and onion with the oil, vinegar, salt and pepper.
Grate the feta over the top in a thick blanket rather than crumbling it through — that is what makes it shopska.
Scatter with parsley and serve with bread.

name: Olivier salad
steps: Boil the potato and carrot in salted water for 12 minutes, adding the peas for the last 2. Drain and cool completely.
Boil the eggs 9 minutes, cool, peel and dice.
Cut everything to roughly the same small dice — this is a salad defined by its uniformity.
Fold through the mayonnaise, yogurt, mustard, pickles, dill and green onions, and season.
Chill an hour before eating. Serve with rye bread.

name: Cottage cheese pancakes
steps: Drain the cottage cheese in a sieve if it is wet, then press it through the sieve so there are no lumps.
Mix with the eggs, sugar, vanilla, salt and most of the flour into a soft, sticky dough.
Shape into small thick patties with floured hands, dusting the outsides.
Fry in the butter over medium-low heat, 4 minutes a side. Low heat matters — high heat browns them before the middle sets.
Serve with sour cream, strawberries and honey.

name: Scallion pancakes
steps: Mix the flour with 150 ml just-boiled water and a teaspoon of salt into a shaggy dough, then knead 5 minutes until smooth. Rest it 15 minutes under a bowl.
Divide in four, roll each thin, brush with sesame oil, scatter with green onions and salt, then roll up into a rope, coil it into a snail and flatten it out again.
That coil is the whole technique — it is what makes the layers.
Fry in the vegetable oil over medium heat, 3 minutes a side, until blistered and golden.
Cut into wedges and serve with the soy sauce, vinegar, chili flakes and ginger stirred together.

name: Wonton soup
steps: Fry the mushrooms until dry, then mix with the tofu, half the green onions, the ginger, garlic, half the soy sauce and the sesame oil.
Put a teaspoon in each wrapper, wet the edges, and fold into a triangle, pressing out the air. Air pockets burst them in the pot.
Simmer the stock with the rest of the soy sauce, the vinegar and chili flakes.
Poach the wontons in a separate pan of gently boiling water for 4 minutes — cooking them in the broth clouds it with starch.
Add the bok choy to the broth for 2 minutes, then lift the wontons in and finish with green onions.

name: Cold spicy noodles
steps: Boil the eggs 8 minutes, then cool, peel and halve.
Cook the noodles, then rinse under cold water until they are genuinely cold, not just cooled.
Whisk the gochujang, vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, soy sauce and garlic.
Toss the noodles through the sauce until evenly red.
Top with the cucumber, kimchi, lettuce, egg, sesame seeds and green onions.

name: Onigiri rice balls
steps: Cook the rice slightly wetter than usual and let it cool until you can just handle it. Warm rice sticks together; cold rice will not hold.
Fry the mushrooms in the vegetable oil until dry, then add the soy sauce, mirin and sesame oil and cook until sticky.
Wet your hands and rub them with salt. Take a handful of rice, press a dip in it, add a little filling of mushroom or cream cheese, and close the rice over it.
Press into a triangle, turning and squeezing until it holds firmly.
Wrap a strip of nori round the base and finish with sesame seeds and green onions.

name: Rolled omelette rice bowl
steps: Cook the rice.
Beat the eggs with the mirin, soy sauce and sugar and strain them if you want it really smooth.
Oil a small pan over medium-low heat and pour in a thin layer. When it is just set on top, roll it to one end.
Oil the pan again, pour in another thin layer, lift the roll so the raw egg runs underneath, and roll it back. Repeat until the egg is used.
Rest 2 minutes, slice thickly, and serve on the rice with the spinach wilted in the hot pan, cucumber, nori, sesame seeds and green onions.

name: Chickpea chaat
steps: Stir the tamarind with the maple syrup and 2 tablespoons of water into a pourable sweet-sour sauce.
Blend most of the cilantro with the chili, lime juice and a splash of water into a green sauce.
Toss the chickpeas, potato and onion with the cumin, chili powder and salt, and fold the pomegranate through.
Pile into bowls and spoon over the yogurt, then both sauces.
Crush the chips over at the very last second. Chaat is assembled to be eaten immediately, not made ahead.

name: Masala omelette with roti
steps: Mix the onion, pepper, chili, cilantro, spices, salt and pepper in a bowl first and let it sit 5 minutes.
Beat the eggs and stir them into the vegetables rather than the other way round, so everything is evenly spread.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat and pour in half the mixture.
Cook 3 minutes, until set underneath and just wet on top, then fold over and give it a minute more. Repeat.
Serve with warm roti and yogurt.

name: Butter beans and lemon on toast
steps: Warm the garlic and chili flakes gently in three quarters of the oil for 2 minutes.
Add the beans with a splash of water and warm through for 5 minutes, crushing about half of them against the pan.
Season hard and stir in the lemon zest and juice off the heat.
Toast the bread and rub it with a cut garlic clove.
Pile the beans on, top with arugula, parmesan, parsley and the rest of the oil.

name: Molletes
steps: Heat the grill. Mash the beans with the cumin, oil and salt in a pan over low heat until thick and spreadable.
Butter the cut rolls and toast them under the grill until just golden.
Spread thickly with the beans and cover with the cheese.
Grill 4 minutes until the cheese bubbles and browns at the edges.
Mix the roasted peppers, radish, onion, chili, lime and cilantro into a rough salsa and spoon it over at the table.

name: Waldorf salad
steps: Toss the diced apple in half the lemon juice straight away, so it does not brown.
Mix the yogurt, mayonnaise, the rest of the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Fold the apple, celery and grapes through the dressing.
Serve on the lettuce with the walnuts and blue cheese scattered over. Add the walnuts last or they soften.

name: Cobb-style salad
steps: Fry the tempeh in the vegetable oil with the paprika, soy sauce and maple syrup until dark and sticky, 8 minutes. This is what stands in for the bacon.
Boil the eggs 8 minutes, cool, peel and quarter.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, mustard and pepper into a dressing.
Lay the lettuce out and arrange the toppings in stripes across it rather than tossing them — a Cobb is a composed salad.
Spoon the dressing over at the table.

name: Tempeh, lettuce and avocado sandwich
steps: Mix the soy sauce, maple syrup and paprika and turn the tempeh slices through it.
Fry in the oil over medium heat, 4 minutes a side, until the edges are dark and crisp. Watch the last minute — the syrup burns quickly.
Toast the bread and spread it with mayonnaise.
Salt the avocado slices and grind pepper over them.
Build with lettuce, pickles, tempeh and avocado, and press down before cutting.

name: Mushroom gravy over split scones
steps: Brown the mushrooms hard in half the butter over high heat, 8 minutes, until they squeak and colour.
Add the onion and the rest of the butter for 5 minutes, then the garlic and thyme.
Stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then add the milk a splash at a time, stirring, until smooth.
Simmer 5 minutes until it coats a spoon, then add the soy sauce and a great deal of black pepper — this gravy should taste peppery, not mild.
Warm and split the scones and ladle the gravy over. Finish with chives.

name: Cheese grits with collards
steps: Bring the milk and stock to a simmer and rain in the polenta, whisking.
Cook 20 minutes on the lowest heat, stirring often. Anything less and it tastes of raw cornmeal.
Meanwhile fry the garlic and chili flakes in the oil, add the collards and a splash of water, and cook 8 minutes until tender. Finish with the vinegar.
Beat the butter and cheese into the grits and season hard.
Spoon the greens over, with a fried egg on top if you want it to go further.

name: Roast beets with labneh
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C. Toss the beets with half the oil, the cumin and salt, and roast 30 minutes until tender at the centre.
Spread the labneh over a plate in a thick swoosh.
Pile the warm beets on — warm against cold is most of the pleasure here.
Drizzle with the pomegranate molasses, the rest of the oil and the lemon juice.
Scatter with walnuts, mint, dill and pepper, and serve with warm pita.

name: Fennel, orange and olive salad
steps: Shave the fennel as thinly as you can and drop it into iced water for 10 minutes to crisp up.
Segment the oranges over a bowl and keep the juice that runs out.
Whisk that juice with the oil, vinegar, salt and pepper.
Toss the drained fennel, orange, olives, onion and arugula through the dressing.
Finish with pistachios and ricotta and serve with bread.

name: Pea and mint soup
steps: Sweat the leek in the butter for 6 minutes without colouring it.
Add the potato, garlic and stock and simmer 10 minutes until the potato is soft.
Add the peas and cook 3 minutes only. Longer and both the colour and the sweetness go.
Blend with the mint until smooth, then season and sharpen with lemon.
Serve with a spoonful of yogurt and bread.

name: Roasted red pepper soup
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and paprika.
Add the peppers, potato and stock and simmer 18 minutes.
The potato is there as the thickener — it is what lets this be creamy without much cream.
Blend completely smooth, season, and stir in the cream if using.
Serve with basil and bread.

name: Corn chowder
steps: Soften the onion and celery in the butter for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and paprika.
Stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then add the stock gradually, whisking.
Add the potato and simmer 12 minutes.
Add the corn and milk and cook 5 minutes more. Blend about a third of the pot and stir it back in for body.
Season and finish with chives and cheddar.

name: Semolina halva
steps: Melt the butter and fry the cashews and raisins until the nuts are golden, then lift them out.
Add the semolina and stir over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, until it smells toasted and turns a shade darker.
Warm the milk with 300 ml water and the sugar separately.
Pour the hot liquid in all at once, standing back — it spits violently. Stir hard until it thickens.
Cook 3 minutes more, fold in the cardamom, nuts and raisins, and rest 5 minutes before serving warm.

name: Apricot and pistachio bites
steps: Blitz or chop the apricots with half the pistachios until they clump together.
Work in the oats, honey, cardamom, lemon zest and salt.
If it will not hold when squeezed, add a little more honey; if it is sticky, more oats.
Roll into about twenty balls and press each into the sesame seeds and the rest of the pistachios, chopped.
Chill 30 minutes. They keep a fortnight in the fridge.

name: Cheese straws
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C and line two trays.
Roll the pastry out thin and brush it with the mustard and half the egg.
Scatter both cheeses, the paprika and the pepper over one half, fold the other half on top, and roll gently to press them together.
Cut into 1 cm strips, twist each a few times, and lay them on the trays pressing the ends down so they hold the twist.
Brush with the rest of the egg, scatter with sesame seeds, and bake 15 minutes until deep gold. Cool on a rack or they go soft.

name: Marinated feta
steps: Toast the fennel seeds and chili flakes in a dry pan for 30 seconds.
Pack the feta into a jar with the garlic, lemon zest, herbs, toasted spices and pepper.
Pour the oil over until everything is submerged.
Leave at room temperature for two hours, or in the fridge for up to a week — take it out an hour before eating, since cold oil sets solid.
Serve with bread, and keep the leftover oil for dressing.

name: Quick pickled vegetables
steps: Warm the vinegar with 150 ml water, the sugar and salt until they dissolve, then take it off the heat.
Pack the vegetables tightly into jars with the mustard seeds, ginger and chili.
Pour the warm brine over to cover. Warm, not boiling — boiling brine cooks the vegetables and you lose the snap.
Cool, then refrigerate at least an hour. Ready in an hour, better the next day, good for three weeks.

name: Beet hummus
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C and roast the beet wedges with a little oil for 30 minutes, until completely soft.
Blend them with the chickpeas, tahini, garlic, lemon juice, cumin and salt.
Add ice-cold water a tablespoon at a time while the motor runs — cold water is what whips hummus pale and light rather than stiff.
Keep going for a full two minutes; it gets smoother the longer you leave it.
Spread in a bowl, pour the oil over, and scatter with pistachios. Serve with pita.

name: Green herb yogurt dip
steps: Blitz the herbs, green onions, chili, garlic, lemon juice, cumin, oil and salt into a coarse green paste.
Fold it through the yogurt rather than blending the yogurt itself, which turns it thin.
Taste for salt and lemon — herb dips need more of both than seems right.
Chill 20 minutes and serve with the carrot and cucumber batons.

name: Corn fritters
steps: Whisk the flour, baking powder, eggs, milk, cumin, salt and pepper into a thick batter.
Blitz or crush a third of the corn and fold it in with the rest whole — the crushed part binds, the whole part pops.
Add the green onions, chili and cilantro.
Fry heaped spoonfuls in the oil over medium heat, 3 minutes a side, without crowding the pan.
Drain on paper and serve hot with sour cream and lime.

name: Onion bhaji
steps: Toss the sliced onions with the salt and leave 15 minutes. They release enough water to make the batter — do not add any.
Add the chickpea flour, spices and cilantro and mix with your hands until the onions are just coated and clinging.
Heat the oil to the point where a scrap of batter sizzles and rises immediately.
Lower in loose clumps and fry 4 minutes, turning, until deep brown. Crowding drops the temperature and makes them greasy, so do a few at a time.
Drain on paper, salt again, and serve with the yogurt blended with mint and lemon.

name: Olive and rosemary focaccia bites
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Warm the oil gently with the garlic and rosemary for 2 minutes, then take it off the heat.
Cut the focaccia into squares and lay them cut side up on a tray.
Brush with the herb oil and bake 8 minutes until the edges crisp.
Toss the roasted peppers and olives with the vinegar and remaining oil and spoon over. Finish with salt and pepper.

name: Chocolate avocado mousse
steps: Melt the chocolate in a bowl over barely simmering water and let it cool for a minute.
Blend the avocados with the maple syrup, milk, vanilla, cinnamon and salt until completely smooth. Stop when there is no trace of green fleck left, or it will taste of avocado.
Add the melted chocolate and blend again briefly.
Chill at least an hour to set.
Serve with the raspberries and pistachios.

name: Roasted grapes with ricotta
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C.
Toss the grapes with the oil, thyme and a pinch of salt and roast 20 minutes, until some have burst and the juices are syrupy.
Beat the ricotta with a spoonful of the honey until it loosens.
Toast the bread.
Spread the ricotta thickly, spoon the grapes and their juices over, and finish with walnuts, the rest of the honey and plenty of black pepper.

name: Apple and oat crumble
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C.
Toss the apples with the lemon juice, a third of the sugar and half the cinnamon, and tip into a dish.
Rub the butter into the flour with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs, then stir in the oats, walnuts, the rest of the sugar and cinnamon, and the salt.
Scatter it over loosely rather than pressing it down — packed crumble steams instead of crisping.
Bake 30 minutes until the top is golden and the fruit bubbles at the edges. Serve with yogurt.

name: Watermelon and mint granita
steps: Blend the watermelon with the lime juice, sugar, half the mint and the salt until smooth.
Pour into a shallow metal tray — shallow and metal, because depth and plastic both slow the freezing and give you a solid block.
Freeze 1 hour, then scrape the whole surface with a fork.
Repeat every 30 minutes for about 3 hours, until it is all loose icy flakes.
Serve in cold glasses with the rest of the mint shredded over.

name: Banana oat cookies
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a tray.
Mash the bananas thoroughly — they are the only binder, so lumps mean cookies that fall apart.
Mix in everything else and let it stand 5 minutes for the oats to take up the moisture.
Spoon onto the tray and flatten each one; they do not spread.
Bake 15 minutes until set and golden at the edges. They keep three days.

name: Sesame honey bars
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for 4 minutes, shaking constantly, until golden and fragrant.
Warm the honey, sugar, lemon juice and salt until bubbling, then cook 4 minutes to a light caramel.
Stir in the seeds, pistachios and cardamom quickly and tip onto baking paper.
Press flat with a second sheet on top, to about 1 cm thick.
Score into bars while still warm; they shatter if you wait until cold. Cool completely before breaking apart.

name: Cheese with figs and honey
steps: Take the cheeses out of the fridge a full hour before serving. Cold cheese tastes of almost nothing.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan and let them cool.
Arrange the cheeses on a board with the figs and grapes, leaving space around each.
Drizzle the honey over the blue cheese only and grind pepper over it.
Serve with crackers and bread.

name: Garlic and herb bread
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Beat the butter with the garlic, parsley, chili flakes, lemon zest and salt.
Cut the baguette almost through at 2 cm intervals, leaving the base attached.
Push the butter into every cut, right to the bottom, and scatter the parmesan over the top.
Wrap in foil and bake 10 minutes, then open the foil for 4 more so the top crisps.

name: Roasted carrot and tahini dip
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the carrots and unpeeled garlic with half the oil, the cumin, paprika and salt.
Roast 30 minutes, until the edges caramelise. The browning is the flavour — pale carrots make a dull dip.
Squeeze the garlic out of its skins and blend with the carrots, tahini, lemon juice and honey.
Loosen with cold water until it is spoonable rather than stiff.
Spread out, pour the rest of the oil over, and top with pumpkin seeds and cilantro. Serve with pita.

name: Miso soup with tofu and wakame
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 15 minutes with the shiitake still in, then strain or leave them, as you prefer.
Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes; it swells to several times its size, so a small pinch is plenty.
Add the tofu and drained wakame and warm through without boiling.
Take the pan off the heat, whisk the miso with a ladle of broth in a cup and stir it back in. Boiled miso goes grainy and flat. Serve with rice and green onions.

name: Miso soup with mushrooms
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 12 minutes, then add the cremini and cook 5 minutes more.
Add the tofu and warm through.
Off the heat, whisk the miso with a ladle of broth and stir it back in.
Serve with rice and a heap of green onions.

name: Miso soup with potato and onion
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Add the potato and onion and simmer 15 minutes, until the potato is soft enough to break with a spoon.
This version is a meal rather than a starter — the potato thickens the broth slightly as it cooks.
Off the heat, whisk the miso with a ladle of broth and stir it back in.
Serve with rice and green onions.

name: Shoyu ramen
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Char the onion halves and ginger in a dry pan until blackened in patches, then add them to the broth with the garlic and simmer 25 minutes.
Boil the eggs 6½ minutes exactly, cool them hard under running water, then peel and halve — the jammy yolk is the point and thirty seconds either way loses it.
Brown the tofu in the vegetable oil. Season the strained broth with the soy sauce, mirin and sake.
Cook the noodles separately so their starch does not cloud the broth, divide between bowls, and ladle the broth over. Top with tofu, egg, sprouts, nori, green onions and sesame oil.

name: Miso ramen with corn and butter
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer the broth 25 minutes. Boil the eggs 6½ minutes and cool them hard.
Fry the garlic, ginger and chili flakes in the oil, add the miso and cook a minute, then whisk in ladles of the hot broth until smooth.
Brown the tofu and blister the corn in a dry pan until it catches in places.
Cook the noodles separately, ladle the miso broth over, and finish each bowl with a knob of butter, the corn, tofu, egg, sprouts and green onions.

name: Spicy sesame ramen
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer the broth 25 minutes. Boil the eggs 6½ minutes and cool them hard.
Fry the crumbled tofu in the vegetable oil over high heat with half the garlic and the gochujang until dark and chewy, 8 minutes.
Whisk the tahini, miso, soy sauce, vinegar, chili flakes and the rest of the garlic and ginger in the bottom of each bowl, then ladle in the hot broth and stir until it goes opaque.
Cook the noodles and blanch the bok choy in the same water. Assemble with the tofu, egg, green onions, sesame oil and seeds.

name: Kake udon
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 20 minutes, then strain.
Season with the soy sauce, mirin, sake and salt. The broth should taste slightly too mild on its own — the noodles carry no salt of their own and will flatten it.
Wilt the spinach in the broth, then loosen the udon in hot water and divide between bowls.
Ladle the broth over and finish with green onions, ginger and nori.

name: Kitsune udon
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 20 minutes and strain.

Pour boiling water over the fried tofu pouches in a sieve to wash off the surface oil, then simmer them in 200 ml of the broth with the sugar and a third of the soy sauce and mirin for 10 minutes, until sweet and saturated.
Season the rest of the broth with the remaining soy sauce, mirin and salt, and wilt the spinach in it.
Divide the udon between bowls, ladle over the broth, and lay the glossy tofu pouches on top with the green onions and ginger.

name: Curry udon
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 20 minutes, strain, and season with the soy sauce, mirin and salt.
Fry the onion in the butter for 10 minutes, stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then the curry powder for 1.
Whisk the hot broth in a ladle at a time until smooth and thickened — all at once and it lumps.
Add the tofu, warm through, and pour over the loosened udon. Curry udon splashes; a spoon is not cheating. Finish with green onions.

name: Kake soba
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 20 minutes, strain, and season with the soy sauce, mirin, sake and salt.
Cook the soba in a separate pan of unsalted water and rinse it briefly — soba sheds a lot of starch and it will turn the broth into gravy.
Wilt the spinach in the broth.
Divide the noodles between bowls, ladle the hot broth over, and top with green onions, nori and sesame seeds.

name: Tempura soba
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 20 minutes, strain and season with the soy sauce, mirin and salt.
Whisk the flour, cornstarch and egg into 250 ml of ice-cold water, barely — lumps are correct. An overworked tempura batter goes bready.
Pour the oil about 2 cm deep and heat it until a drop of batter sinks and rises immediately. Fry the vegetables in small batches for 2-3 minutes until pale gold, and drain them standing up on a rack.
Cook and rinse the soba, ladle the broth over, and sit the tempura on top at the very last second so it is still crisp when it reaches the table.

name: Oroshi soba
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 20 minutes, strain, and season with the soy sauce, mirin and salt.
Grate the daikon finely and drain it in a sieve, pressing lightly. Keep it raw — cooked, it loses the clean pepperiness the whole dish is built on.
Cook and rinse the soba.
Ladle the broth over, heap the grated daikon in the middle, and finish with lemon, green onions, nori and sesame seeds.

name: Agedashi tofu
steps: Drain the tofu on paper for 10 minutes and cut it into thick cubes. Handle it as little as you can bear.

Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 15 minutes, strain, and season with the soy sauce and mirin.
Roll the tofu in cornstarch just before frying — coated early, the starch goes wet and slides off.
Fry in the hot oil for 3 minutes, until the crust is set and pale. Sit the cubes in shallow bowls, pour the hot broth around rather than over, and top with ginger and green onions. Serve with rice.

name: Agedashi tofu with mushroom sauce
steps: Drain the tofu on paper for 10 minutes and cut into thick cubes.

Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 12 minutes with the cremini added, season with the soy sauce and mirin, then thicken with 2 teaspoons of the cornstarch slaked in cold water until the sauce turns glossy and clings.
Roll the tofu in the remaining cornstarch and fry 3 minutes in the hot oil.
Spoon the mushroom sauce over and finish with ginger and green onions. Serve with rice.

name: Agedashi tofu with grated daikon
steps: Drain the tofu on paper for 10 minutes and cut into thick cubes.

Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 15 minutes, strain, and season with the soy sauce and mirin.
Grate the daikon and drain it lightly.

Roll the tofu in cornstarch, fry 3 minutes, and sit it in the broth with a heap of daikon on each piece. The daikon cuts the fried coating, which is the whole reason it is there. Serve with rice and nori.

name: Vegetable tempura with rice
steps: Start the rice. Mix the soy sauce and mirin with 150 ml water for the dipping sauce and grate the daikon into it.
Whisk the flour, cornstarch and egg into 300 ml ice-cold water with barely a dozen strokes. Lumps are correct; a smooth batter makes heavy tempura.
Pour the oil about 2 cm deep and heat it until a drop of batter sinks and comes straight back up.
Dip the vegetables and fry in small batches for 2-3 minutes, until pale gold rather than brown. Crowding the pan drops the temperature and the batter drinks oil.
Drain on a rack, salt immediately, and serve with the rice and dipping sauce.

name: Sweet potato and squash tempura
steps: Start the rice and mix the dipping sauce from the soy sauce, mirin, 150 ml water and the grated daikon.
Slice the sweet potato and squash thinly and evenly — thick slices stay raw inside a coating that is already too dark.
Whisk the batter briefly with ice-cold water, leaving it lumpy.
Fry in batches for 3-4 minutes, a little longer than soft vegetables need.
Drain on a rack, salt at once, and serve with the rice and sauce.

name: Mushroom and green bean tempura
steps: Start the rice and mix the dipping sauce.
Wipe the mushrooms rather than washing them — wet mushrooms spit in the oil and shed their coating.
Whisk the batter briefly with ice-cold water.
Fry in batches 2-3 minutes. Hold three or four beans together as you lower them in and they fry as one crisp raft.
Drain on a rack, salt immediately, and serve with rice and the sauce.

name: Vegetable chirashi bowl
steps: Cook the sushi rice and, while it is hot, fold through the vinegar, sugar and salt with a cutting rather than stirring motion, then spread it out to cool to body temperature.
Beat the eggs and cook them as a thin sheet in the oil, roll it and slice into fine ribbons.
Boil the edamame 4 minutes and cool.
Spread the rice in four shallow bowls.

Lay the toppings over it in blocks rather than mixing them in — chirashi means scattered, and the pleasure is taking a different combination with each mouthful. Finish with soy sauce, sesame oil, seeds and nori.

name: Chirashi bowl with marinated tofu
steps: Cook the sushi rice and season it with the vinegar, sugar and salt while hot, then cool it.
Press the tofu dry and marinate the slices in the soy sauce and mirin for 10 minutes.
Fry them in the oil over high heat until the marinade caramelises on both sides, 6 minutes.
Spread the rice in bowls and lay the tofu, avocado, cucumber and carrot over in blocks.
Finish with sesame oil, seeds and nori.

name: Chirashi bowl with simmered mushrooms
steps: Cook and season the sushi rice, then cool it.
Simmer both mushrooms with the soy sauce, mirin, sake and 100 ml water for 12 minutes, until the liquid has almost gone and they are glossy and dark.
Cook the beaten eggs as a thin sheet and slice into ribbons.
Spread the rice in bowls and arrange the mushrooms, egg, cucumber and carrot in blocks.
Finish with sesame seeds and nori.

name: Inari sushi
steps: Pour boiling water over the pouches in a sieve to wash off the surface oil, then press them gently between your palms.
Simmer them in 250 ml water with the soy sauce, mirin and sugar for 15 minutes, until they have drunk nearly all of it. Let them cool in what is left.
Cook the sushi rice and season it with the vinegar, salt and sesame seeds while hot.
Open each pouch into a bag — rolling it back on itself first stops it tearing — and fill loosely with rice.
Fold the opening under and sit them seam-down. They keep a day and travel better than almost anything else.

name: Inari sushi with carrot and sesame
steps: Rinse the pouches in boiling water and press them dry.
Simmer them in 250 ml water with the soy sauce, mirin and sugar for 15 minutes and cool in the liquid.
Cook the sushi rice, adding the diced carrot for the last 5 minutes so it steams soft with the grains.
Season the hot rice with the vinegar, salt, sesame seeds and sesame oil.
Open the pouches, fill loosely, and fold the openings under.

name: Inari sushi with edamame
steps: Rinse the pouches in boiling water and press dry.
Simmer in 250 ml water with the soy sauce, mirin and sugar for 15 minutes and cool in the liquid.
Boil the edamame 4 minutes, cool, and chop them roughly.
Season the hot sushi rice with the vinegar and salt, then fold through the edamame, sesame seeds and green onions.
Fill the pouches loosely and fold the openings under.

name: Miso walnut onigiri
steps: Cook the rice and let it cool until you can just handle it.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan, then stir in the miso, mirin, sugar and sesame oil and cook 2 minutes to a thick paste.
Wet your hands and rub them with salt. Press a dip into a handful of rice, add a little paste, and close the rice over it.
Shape into a triangle, turning and squeezing until it holds.
Wrap a strip of nori round the base and scatter with green onions.

name: Edamame sesame onigiri
steps: Cook the rice and let it cool until handleable.
Boil the edamame 4 minutes, cool, and chop roughly.
Fold the edamame, sesame seeds, sesame oil, soy sauce and green onions through the warm rice.
Wet and salt your hands, then press handfuls into firm triangles.
Wrap with nori just before eating so it stays crisp.

name: Japanese potato salad
steps: Salt the cucumber and onion in a sieve for 10 minutes, then squeeze them dry.
Boil the potatoes and carrot in salted water for 18 minutes, until the potato is falling apart at the edges.
Drain, and while still steaming, mash about half of it roughly and fold the vinegar through. Hot potato takes up the acid; cold potato only wears it.
Boil the eggs 9 minutes, cool, peel and chop.
Fold everything through the mayonnaise, season hard, and chill. Better the next day.

name: Japanese potato salad with corn
steps: Salt the cucumber in a sieve for 10 minutes and squeeze it dry.
Boil the potatoes 18 minutes, drain, and mash half of them roughly while hot with the vinegar.
Blister the corn in a dry hot pan for 4 minutes so it tastes of something.
Fold everything through the mayonnaise with the green onions and season well.
Chill before serving.

name: Kinpira carrot and daikon
steps: Cut everything into matchsticks of the same thickness — kinpira is a dish about texture and uneven pieces ruin it.
Get the pan hot with the vegetable oil and stir-fry the vegetables for 4 minutes without letting them soften completely.
Add the chili flakes, then the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar.
Cook hard for 5 minutes until the liquid has gone and what is left clings and glazes.
Off the heat, add the sesame oil and seeds. Good hot, better at room temperature, and it keeps four days. Serve with rice.

name: Kinpira green beans and carrot
steps: Cut the beans into lengths that match the carrot matchsticks.
Stir-fry both in the vegetable oil over high heat for 5 minutes, until blistered but still squeaky.
Add the chili flakes, soy sauce, mirin and sugar.
Cook until the pan is dry and the glaze clings, about 5 minutes.
Finish off the heat with sesame oil and seeds. Serve with rice.

name: Spinach ohitashi
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 10 minutes, strain, season with the soy sauce and mirin, and cool completely.
Blanch the spinach for 40 seconds only, then plunge it straight into cold water.
Squeeze it out hard into a tight log and cut into short lengths, so it stays in neat bundles rather than collapsing into a mat.
Sit the bundles in the cold broth for at least 20 minutes and serve with the broth spooned over and sesame seeds on top.

name: Green bean ohitashi
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 10 minutes, strain, season and cool completely.
Boil the beans 4 minutes, until they have lost their squeak but not their colour, then cool them in iced water.
Drain well and steep in the cold broth at least 30 minutes.
Serve cold with the broth and sesame seeds.

name: Broccoli ohitashi
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 10 minutes, strain, season and cool.
Boil the broccoli 3 minutes and cool it in iced water so it stays bright.
Steep in the cold broth 30 minutes.
Serve with the broth, sesame seeds and a few drops of sesame oil.

name: Spinach goma-ae
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for 3 minutes, until they smell strong and start to jump.
Grind most of them to a coarse, oily paste in a mortar, keeping a spoonful whole. Grinding is what makes goma-ae rather than spinach with seeds on.
Stir in the soy sauce, mirin and sugar.
Blanch the spinach 40 seconds, cool in cold water and squeeze very dry.
Toss through the sesame dressing and top with the whole seeds.

name: Green bean goma-ae
steps: Toast the sesame seeds until fragrant and grind most of them to a coarse paste.
Stir in the soy sauce, mirin and sugar.
Boil the beans 4 minutes and cool them in iced water.
