Dry them thoroughly — wet beans thin the dressing and it slides off.
Toss through the dressing and finish with the reserved whole seeds.

name: Broccoli goma-ae
steps: Toast and grind the sesame seeds, keeping a spoonful whole.
Stir in the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and vinegar.
Boil the broccoli 3 minutes and cool it in iced water.
Drain and dry it well.
Toss through the dressing and scatter the whole seeds over.

name: Yasai itame
steps: Start the rice. Have every vegetable cut before the pan goes on; there is no pause once it starts.
Get the pan as hot as it goes with the vegetable oil. Add the hard vegetables — onion, carrot, cabbage stems — and leave them alone for 2 minutes.
Add the pepper and cabbage leaves for 2 minutes, then the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the sprouts, soy sauce and sake and toss for one minute only. Sprouts go limp fast and their snap is the whole texture of the dish.
Off the heat, add the sesame oil, salt and a lot of pepper, and serve over rice.

name: Yasai itame with tofu
steps: Start the rice. Press the tofu dry and brown it hard in half the oil, then lift it out.
Stir-fry the onion, carrot and cabbage in the rest of the oil for 4 minutes over the highest heat.
Add the garlic and ginger, then the sprouts.
Return the tofu with the soy sauce, sake and the cornstarch slaked in a splash of water, and toss until it glazes.
Finish with sesame oil and pepper and serve over rice.

name: Yasai itame with mushrooms
steps: Start the rice.
Brown both mushrooms hard in the oil in two batches — crowded, they steam, and this dish lives on their browning.
Add the carrot and cabbage for 3 minutes, then the garlic and ginger.
Return the mushrooms with the sprouts, soy sauce and sake and toss for a minute.
Finish with sesame oil, green onions and pepper, and serve over rice.

name: Yosenabe hot pot
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 20 minutes with the ginger, then season with the soy sauce, mirin, sake and salt.
Add the vegetables in order of how long they need — daikon and carrot first, then the cabbage stems, then the leaves.
Slide the tofu in and let it warm through without stirring.
Add the udon at the very end. A nabe is meant to be eaten from the pot as it goes, so put it on the table and let people help themselves. Finish with green onions.

name: Kimchi nabe
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 20 minutes and strain.
Fry the kimchi with the garlic and gochujang in a dry pot for 4 minutes until the edges caramelise, then pour the broth in with the soy sauce and mirin.
Add the carrot and cabbage and simmer until tender, then slide in the tofu.
Add the udon at the end and finish with green onions and sesame oil.

name: Miso nabe
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 20 minutes with the garlic and ginger, then strain.
Add the potato and carrot and cook 10 minutes, then the cabbage.
Whisk the miso and mirin with a ladle of the broth in a cup and stir it back in off the boil — a nabe kept at a rolling boil after the miso goes in turns grey and grainy.
Add the tofu and udon, warm through, and finish with green onions, sesame oil and a knob of butter if you want it richer.

name: Yakisoba
steps: Cook the noodles just short of done, drain and toss with a teaspoon of the oil so they do not weld together.
Mix the hoisin, soy sauce, vinegar and sriracha into a sauce.
Get the pan very hot. Fry the onion, carrot and cabbage in the rest of the oil for 5 minutes, leaving them alone between stirs so they char.
Add the noodles and press them into the pan, letting them catch, then pour the sauce round the edge rather than into the middle so it hits hot metal and caramelises.
Toss in the sprouts for thirty seconds and serve with mayonnaise, nori, green onions and pepper.

name: Mushroom yakisoba
steps: Cook the noodles just short and toss with a little oil.
Brown both mushrooms hard in the oil, in two batches, then set aside.
Fry the carrot and cabbage for 4 minutes over high heat.
Return the mushrooms with the noodles, press them into the pan to catch, and add the sauce round the edge.
Toss in the sprouts at the last second and serve with mayonnaise, nori, green onions and pepper.

name: Tofu yakisoba
steps: Cook the noodles just short and toss with a little oil.
Press the tofu dry and brown it hard in half the oil until crisp on several sides, then lift out.
Fry the cabbage and carrot in the rest of the oil for 5 minutes over high heat.
Add the noodles, press them flat to catch, pour the sauce round the edge, and return the tofu.
Toss in the sprouts and serve with mayonnaise, nori, green onions and pepper.

name: Potato korokke
steps: Start the rice. Boil the potatoes 20 minutes, drain, and let them steam dry before mashing — wet mash will burst in the oil.
Fry the onion in the butter for 10 minutes until sweet and golden, then fold it through the mash with plenty of salt and pepper. Cool it completely.
Shape into eight flat patties. Dredge in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing the crumbs on firmly.
Shallow-fry in 2 cm of hot oil for 3 minutes, turning once, until deep gold. They are already cooked through, so this is about the crust only.
Drain on a rack and serve with the raw shredded cabbage, hoisin sauce and rice.

name: Squash korokke
steps: Start the rice. Steam or boil the squash and potato together for 18 minutes and drain very well.
Squash holds far more water than potato, so let it steam dry in the pan for a few minutes before mashing or the patties will not hold.
Fry the onion in the butter for 10 minutes and fold it through the mash with the cinnamon, salt and pepper. Cool completely.
Shape, then coat in flour, egg and panko.
Fry 3 minutes until deep gold, drain on a rack, and serve with the cabbage, hoisin and rice.

name: Corn korokke
steps: Start the rice. Boil and mash the potatoes, letting them steam dry first.
Fry the onion in the butter for 10 minutes, add the corn for 3, and fold through the mash with salt and pepper. Cool completely.
Shape into eight patties and coat in flour, egg and panko.
Fry 3 minutes until deep gold. Corn pops in hot oil, so keep the patties well sealed in crumb and stand back.
Drain on a rack and serve with the cabbage, hoisin and rice.

name: Chawanmushi
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 15 minutes, strain and cool to lukewarm. Hot broth would scramble the eggs.
Beat the eggs gently — no bubbles — and stir in 400 ml of the broth with the soy sauce, mirin and salt. Strain the mixture; this one step is the difference between silk and rubber.
Pour into cups, cover each with foil, and steam over low heat for 15 minutes. The surface should wobble as one piece.
Rest 2 minutes and top with green onions.

name: Chawanmushi with mushrooms
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 15 minutes, lift out the shiitake and keep them, then cool the broth to lukewarm.
Beat the eggs without frothing them, stir in 400 ml broth with the soy sauce, mirin and salt, and strain.
Divide the mushrooms between the cups and pour the custard over.
Cover and steam 15 minutes on low heat until set with a single soft wobble. Finish with green onions.

name: Chawanmushi with edamame
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth slimy and bitter, and the twenty minutes of gentle heat is where all the savour comes from.
Simmer 15 minutes, strain and cool to lukewarm.
Boil the edamame 4 minutes and cool them.
Beat the eggs gently, stir in 400 ml broth with the soy sauce, mirin and salt, and strain.
Divide the edamame between cups, pour the custard over, cover and steam 15 minutes. Finish with green onions.

name: Hiyayakko
steps: Drain the tofu and chill it thoroughly. This is a dish with nowhere to hide, so it has to be properly cold.
Turn it out and cut into two thick blocks.
Heap the ginger and green onions on top.
Pour the soy sauce over at the table rather than in advance, or it draws water out of the tofu and pools.
Finish with sesame oil, seeds and nori.

name: Hiyayakko with tomato
steps: Chill the tofu thoroughly and drain it.
Salt the diced tomato and leave it 5 minutes, then use it with the juice it gives up — that liquid is half the dressing.
Stir the soy sauce, vinegar and sesame oil into the tomato.
Cut the tofu into two blocks and spoon the tomato over.
Finish with green onions and sesame seeds.

name: Hiyayakko with grated daikon
steps: Chill and drain the tofu.
Grate the daikon and drain it in a sieve, pressing gently — it holds a surprising amount of water and will flood the plate.
Cut the tofu into two blocks and heap the daikon on top.
Dress with soy sauce, lemon juice and sesame oil.
Finish with green onions, chili flakes and nori.

name: Cucumber tsukemono
steps: Toss the sliced cucumber with the salt and leave 20 minutes in a sieve.
Squeeze it firmly. What comes out is the water that would otherwise dilute everything else.
Mix with the kombu, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce and chili flakes.
Chill at least an hour, pressed under a plate if you can manage it.
Serve cold with the sesame seeds. Keeps four days and gets better for two of them.

name: Daikon tsukemono
steps: Salt the daikon and carrot and leave 20 minutes, then squeeze out the water.
Dissolve the sugar in the vinegar.
Mix everything together with the kombu, chili flakes and lemon zest.
Chill at least two hours — daikon is denser than cucumber and takes longer to take up the brine.
Keeps a week in the fridge.

name: Napa cabbage tsukemono
steps: Toss the cabbage with the salt and leave it 30 minutes under a weight.
Squeeze it out hard — a good double handful of water should come off it.
Mix with the kombu, carrot, ginger, vinegar, sugar and chili flakes.
Press again under a plate and chill overnight if you can.
Keeps five days and sharpens as it goes.

name: Grilled mochi with soy and nori
steps: Grill or dry-pan the mochi over medium heat, turning often, for about 8 minutes.
They puff up dramatically and then collapse — that is the signal they are done, and a fair amount of smoke is normal.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin and sugar.
Dip each hot mochi in the sauce so it hisses, then wrap in a strip of nori.
Eat immediately. Mochi is only itself while it is hot, and turns to rubber within minutes of cooling.

name: Grilled mochi with sweet red bean
steps: Grill or dry-pan the mochi, turning often, for about 8 minutes until they puff and collapse.
Warm the red bean paste with a splash of water and a pinch of salt until spoonable. The salt is not optional — without it the paste tastes flatly sweet.
Sit each mochi in a bowl and spoon the warm paste over.
Dust with matcha if you have it, and eat while hot.

name: Grilled mochi with sugar and soy
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan and crush them roughly with the sugar.
Grill or dry-pan the mochi for about 8 minutes, turning, until puffed and collapsing.
Brush each one with soy sauce while hot.
Roll in the sesame sugar so it sticks to the damp surface.
Eat at once.

name: Matcha milk pudding
steps: Sift the matcha with the sugar and cornstarch. Matcha clumps stubbornly and sifting is the only thing that prevents green specks throughout.
Whisk in a little of the cold milk to make a smooth paste, then the rest.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, whisking constantly, until it thickens to a pouring custard, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the cream, vanilla and salt off the heat.
Pour into four glasses and chill at least 3 hours.

name: Matcha pudding with red bean
steps: Sift the matcha with the sugar and cornstarch, then whisk to a paste with a little cold milk and add the rest.
Simmer, whisking constantly, until it thickens, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the cream and salt off the heat.
Spoon a layer of red bean paste into the bottom of four glasses and pour the pudding over. Less sugar than the plain version, because the paste brings its own.
Chill at least 3 hours.

name: Spinach dal
steps: Simmer the lentils with the turmeric and 1 litre of water for 20 minutes, skimming the foam.
Start the rice.
Fry the onion in the butter for 8 minutes, then the garlic, ginger, cumin and chili flakes for a minute, letting the onion darken for 4 more.
Stir the whole panful into the lentils with the salt.
Add the spinach in handfuls and cook just until it collapses — any longer and it goes khaki. Finish with garam masala and lemon and serve on rice.

name: Squash dal
steps: Simmer the lentils and squash with the turmeric and 900 ml water for 22 minutes, until both collapse.
Start the rice.
Fry the onion in the butter for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, cumin and chili flakes.
Stir the tempering into the lentils with the coconut milk and salt and simmer 5 minutes.
Finish with garam masala and cilantro and serve over rice.

name: Squash and black bean chili
steps: Soften the onion and pepper in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and all the spices — the cinnamon is small but it is what stops this tasting like the bean version.
Add the roasted peppers, squash, beans, stock and salt.
Simmer 28 minutes, until the squash holds its shape but yields completely to a spoon.
Finish with lime and cilantro, and sour cream if you like.

name: Corn and pepper chili
steps: Char the peppers and onion hard in the oil over high heat for 8 minutes so they take colour rather than just softening.
Add the garlic and spices for a minute.
Add the roasted peppers, both beans, stock and salt and simmer 25 minutes.
Blister the corn separately in a dry pan and stir it in for the last 5 minutes, so it stays sweet and distinct.
Finish with lime and cilantro.

name: Chana saag
steps: Fry the onion in the oil for 10 minutes until properly browned at the edges.
Add the garlic, ginger and ground spices, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the yogurt a spoonful at a time with the salt. Cook until the oil separates out.
Add the chickpeas and a splash of water and simmer 12 minutes, crushing a few against the pan.
Wilt the spinach through in handfuls.
Finish with garam masala, lemon and the cream if using, and serve with naan.

name: Chana aloo
steps: Fry the onion in the oil for 10 minutes until browned.
Add the garlic, ginger and ground spices, then the yogurt off the heat, a spoonful at a time, with the salt.
Add the potato, chickpeas and 300 ml water and simmer 20 minutes, until a knife slides into the potato.
Crush a few potatoes against the side to thicken the gravy.
Finish with garam masala, lemon and cilantro, and serve with naan.

name: Winter minestrone
steps: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and rosemary, then the stock, beans, squash and salt. Simmer 18 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook 10 minutes more.
Stir the kale through for the last 5 minutes.
Season hard and serve with parmesan and pepper.

name: Spring minestrone
steps: Sweat the leek and celery in the oil for 8 minutes without colouring them — this version stays pale and light.
Add the garlic, stock, beans and salt and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the pasta and zucchini and cook 8 minutes.
Add the asparagus and peas for the last 3 minutes only.
Finish with lemon zest, a spoonful of pesto in each bowl, parmesan and pepper.

name: Tofu, green bean and peanut stir-fry
steps: Start the rice and press the tofu dry.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, honey, cornstarch and 60 ml water.
Brown the tofu in the vegetable oil over high heat until crisp, then lift out.
Fry the beans hard for 5 minutes until blistered and wrinkled, then add the garlic, ginger and chili flakes.
Return the tofu, pour in the sauce, and toss until it thickens. Finish with peanuts, sesame oil and green onions.

name: Tofu, bok choy and almond stir-fry
steps: Start the rice and press the tofu dry.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, honey, cornstarch and 60 ml water.
Brown the tofu in the oil until crisp and lift out.
Fry the carrot and bok choy stems for 3 minutes, then the leaves and the garlic and ginger for 1 — the stems and leaves need different times and adding them together gives you one of them wrong.
Return the tofu with the sauce and toss until glossy. Finish with almonds, sesame oil and seeds.

name: Tomato and red pepper soup
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and paprika.
Add the tomatoes, peppers, stock and salt.
Simmer 20 minutes — a tomato soup that tastes thin has almost always been rushed.
Blend smooth and stir in the cream if using.
Serve with basil, pepper and bread.

name: Tomato and lentil soup
steps: Soften the onion and carrot in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, cumin and oregano.
Add the tomatoes, lentils, stock and salt.
Simmer 25 minutes, until the lentils have collapsed and thickened the soup.
Blend half of it and stir it back in, or blend it all if you want it smooth.
Sharpen with lemon, season, and serve with bread.

name: Green shakshuka
steps: Sweat the leek and zucchini in the oil for 10 minutes until soft and sweet.
Add the garlic, cumin and chili flakes for a minute.
Wilt the spinach through and cook off any water that collects. A wet base will not hold the eggs.
Make six wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook 6-8 minutes until the whites set.
Scatter with feta and the herbs, squeeze over the lemon, and serve with bread.

name: Butter bean shakshuka
steps: Soften the onion and peppers in the oil for 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and harissa for a minute, then the roasted peppers, stock and salt.
Simmer 10 minutes, then stir in the beans and cook 5 more until thick.
Make six wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook 6-8 minutes.
Scatter with feta and parsley and serve with bread.

name: Leek mac and cheese
steps: Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry pan and set aside.
Sweat the leeks in a third of the butter, covered, for 10 minutes. Keep them pale.
Cook the macaroni. Melt the rest of the butter, stir in the flour, cook 2 minutes, then whisk in the milk gradually and simmer until it coats a spoon.
Off the heat, add both cheeses, the mustard, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Fold through the pasta and leeks and top with the crumbs and thyme.

name: Smoked cheddar mac and cheese
steps: Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry pan and set aside.
Cook the macaroni, adding the spinach for the last 30 seconds, then drain and squeeze out any water the spinach released.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, cook 2 minutes, then whisk in the milk and simmer until thickened.
Take it off the heat before the cheese goes in — smoked cheddar splits more readily than plain, so this matters more here than usual.
Season with mustard, paprika, salt and pepper, fold through the pasta and spinach, and top with the crumbs.

name: Mushroom pizza
steps: Heat the oven as high as it goes with a tray inside.
Toss the mushrooms with a little of the oil and salt and leave them 10 minutes, then squeeze them out. Raw mushrooms release their water onto the base and make it soggy.
Blend the peppers smooth with the oregano and salt for the sauce.
Stretch the dough, spread thinly with sauce, and top with mozzarella, mushrooms, garlic and thyme.
Bake 8-10 minutes on the hot tray and finish with parmesan and the rest of the oil.

name: Potato and rosemary pizza
steps: Heat the oven as high as it will go with a tray inside.
Slice the potatoes as thinly as you possibly can and toss them with half the oil and the salt. Anything thicker than a coin stays raw in the eight minutes a pizza gets.
Stretch the dough. There is no sauce on this one — the potato and cheese are the whole thing.
Lay the potato in overlapping rounds, dot with mozzarella, and scatter the garlic and rosemary.
Bake 8-10 minutes, then finish with parmesan, pepper and the rest of the oil.

name: Pinto burrito bowl
steps: Cook the rice and fork through the lime juice and half the cilantro.
Char the peppers and onion hard in the oil over high heat for 8 minutes.
Add the beans, cumin, salt and a splash of water and warm through.
Build the bowls: rice, then the beans and peppers, then lettuce, salsa, avocado and cheese.
Finish with the rest of the cilantro.

name: Sweet potato burrito bowl
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the sweet potato with the oil, cumin, paprika and salt and roast 28 minutes.
Cook the rice and fork through the lime juice.
Warm the beans through with a splash of water.
Build the bowls with rice, sweet potato, beans, lettuce, salsa, avocado and cheese.
Finish with cilantro and sour cream.

name: Coconut squash and chickpea curry
steps: Start the rice.
Soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and curry powder.
Add the squash, chickpeas, coconut milk and 200 ml water and simmer 22 minutes, until the squash is tender.
Wilt the spinach through at the end.
Finish with lime and cilantro and serve over the rice.

name: Coconut chickpea and green bean curry
steps: Start the rice.
Pop the mustard seeds in the hot oil, then add the onion for 6 minutes and the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1.
Add the chickpeas and coconut milk and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the green beans and cook 6 minutes more — they should still have some bite against the soft chickpeas.
Finish with lime and cilantro and serve over rice.

name: Potato and fennel soup
steps: Toast the fennel seeds in the butter for 30 seconds, then add the leek and fennel and sweat, covered, for 12 minutes.
Keep them pale — browning turns the fennel bitter and this soup wants to taste sweet and clean.
Add the garlic, potato and stock and simmer 18 minutes.
Blend smooth, stir in the cream, and sharpen with a little lemon.
Season hard and serve with bread.

name: Potato, leek and kale soup
steps: Sweat the leeks in the butter for 10 minutes, then add the garlic and chili flakes.
Add the potato and stock and simmer 18 minutes.
Blend about half the pot and stir it back in, so it is thick but still has pieces in it.
Add the beans and kale and cook 5 minutes more.
Season, finish each bowl with the olive oil and pepper, and serve with bread.

name: Greek salad with chickpeas
steps: Soak the sliced onion in cold water for 5 minutes to take the bite out, then drain.
Turn the chickpeas through the oil, lemon and oregano first and leave them 5 minutes — they take up dressing in a way the vegetables will not.
Add the cucumber, pepper, onion and olives.
Fold through the lettuce and feta and grind over plenty of pepper.

name: Watermelon Greek salad
steps: Salt the watermelon lightly and leave it 5 minutes, then tip away the liquid that collects.
Soak the onion in cold water for 5 minutes and drain.
Layer the watermelon, cucumber, pepper, onion and olives.
Dress with the oil, lemon and oregano. Go easy on any extra salt — the feta and olives bring plenty.
Finish with mint, feta and a lot of black pepper.

name: Roasted red pepper hummus
steps: Drain the peppers well and pat them dry, or the hummus turns watery and pale.
Blend the chickpeas, peppers, tahini, garlic, lemon juice, cumin and salt.
Add ice-cold water a spoonful at a time with the motor running and keep going a full two minutes — it is time, not liquid, that makes hummus light.
Spread out, pour the oil over and dust with paprika.
Serve with the carrot and cucumber batons.

name: Herb and lemon hummus
steps: Blend the chickpeas, tahini, garlic, lemon juice, cumin and salt with ice-cold water for two full minutes.
Add the herbs at the very end and pulse only briefly. Blended long, they turn the whole bowl a dull grey-green.
Taste for lemon; a herb hummus wants noticeably more acid than a plain one.
Spread out and pour the oil over.
Serve with the vegetable batons.

name: Mango coconut chia pudding
steps: Whisk the chia seeds into the coconut milk and milk with the maple syrup.
Whisk again after 5 minutes. This second pass is what stops it setting as one lump with dry seeds around it.
Cover and refrigerate at least 3 hours or overnight.
Blend half the mango to a purée with the lime juice and dice the rest.
Layer the pudding with the purée and the diced mango, and top with almonds.

name: Banana peanut butter chia pudding
steps: Mash one banana thoroughly and whisk it into the milk with the peanut butter, maple syrup and cinnamon.
Whisk in the chia seeds, then whisk again after 5 minutes.
Cover and refrigerate at least 3 hours.
Slice the second banana over the top just before serving, or it browns.
Finish with the chopped chocolate.

name: Date and cashew balls
steps: Blitz the cashews until they are coarse crumbs rather than butter.
Add the dates, oats, cinnamon, vanilla and salt and blitz until the mixture clumps when you squeeze it.
If it will not hold, add a date rather than water — water makes them sticky and they will not keep.
Roll into about sixteen balls and press each into the sesame seeds.
Chill 30 minutes. They keep two weeks in the fridge.

name: Apricot and pistachio balls
steps: Blitz half the pistachios to coarse crumbs and chop the rest by hand for texture.
Add the apricots, oats, honey, cardamom, lemon zest and salt and blitz until it clumps.
Roll into about sixteen balls.
Press each into the sesame seeds and the chopped pistachios.
Chill 30 minutes before eating; they keep a fortnight.

name: Cherry tomato, olive and caper spaghetti
steps: Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry pan and set aside; there is no cheese in this one and the crumbs do that job.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water.
Warm the garlic and chili flakes in the oil, then add the olives and capers for a minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook 10-12 minutes until they collapse into a sauce.
Toss the pasta through with a splash of its water, then the basil, crumbs and pepper. Taste before salting — the olives and capers usually cover it.

name: Cherry tomato spaghetti with burrata
steps: Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water.
Warm the garlic and chili flakes in the oil for a minute, then add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt.
Cook 10-12 minutes, pressing them, until they collapse.
Toss the drained pasta through the sauce with a splash of its water and the lemon zest.
Tear the burrata over each plate at the table rather than stirring it in — it should stay in soft pools, and stirred through it just disappears.

name: Mushroom, walnut and sage pasta
steps: Cook the pasta in well-salted water.
Brown both mushrooms hard in the oil in two batches — crowd the pan and they steam, and the browning is the dish.
Add the butter and sage and let it foam until the leaves crisp and the butter smells nutty.
Add the garlic for a minute, then the drained pasta with a good splash of its water.
Toss with the parmesan until it coats, and finish with the walnuts, lemon and plenty of pepper.

name: Mushroom, pea and lemon pasta
steps: Cook the pasta, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes.
Brown the mushrooms hard in the oil, in two batches.
Add the butter and garlic for a minute, then the cream and lemon zest.
Toss the drained pasta and peas through with a splash of the water and the parmesan.
Finish with lemon juice, mint and pepper.

name: Quinoa bowl with beets and goat cheese
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the beets, carrot and onion with three quarters of the oil, the thyme, salt and pepper and roast 32 minutes.
Rinse the quinoa and simmer in twice its volume of water for 15 minutes, then rest covered 5 minutes and fork it through.
Whisk the vinegar, mustard and remaining oil into a dressing.
Toss the warm quinoa with half the dressing and the arugula so it just wilts.
Pile the roasted vegetables on and finish with goat cheese, walnuts and the rest of the dressing.

name: Quinoa bowl with cauliflower and tahini
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the cauliflower, chickpeas and onion with three quarters of the oil, the cumin, paprika and salt and roast 30 minutes.
Rinse the quinoa and simmer 15 minutes, then rest covered and fork it through.
Whisk the tahini with the lemon juice and enough cold water to pour — it will seize first, then loosen.
Fold the spinach through the warm quinoa so it wilts.
Pile the tray contents on top and finish with the tahini, parsley and pomegranate seeds.

name: Cherry tomato spaghetti with ricotta
steps: Beat the ricotta loose with the lemon zest, a grind of pepper and a spoonful of oil. It goes in cold at the end, so this is the whole of the work it needs.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water.
Warm the garlic and chili flakes in the rest of the oil, add the tomatoes and cook 10-12 minutes until they slump.
Toss the drained pasta through the tomatoes with a splash of its water.
Serve with the ricotta spooned over rather than stirred in — it should stay in white pockets against the red, not turn the whole pan pink.

name: Cacio e pepe with lemon
steps: Toast the pepper in a dry wide pan for a minute, until it smells sharp.
Cook the spaghetti in the smallest amount of salted water that covers it, so the water goes starchy. That starch is the sauce.
Add a ladle of the water, the butter and all the lemon zest to the pepper pan and swirl to an emulsion.
Drag the pasta across a minute short of done, take the pan off the heat entirely, then add the cheese and toss hard.
Juice half the lemon in at the very end. Adding it earlier curdles the cheese — acid and a hot pan are what break this sauce.

name: Cacio e pepe with zucchini
steps: Fry the zucchini coins in the oil in batches over high heat until deeply golden on both sides, then salt them and set aside. Crowding the pan steams them, and steamed zucchini will not hold up in a sauce.
Toast the pepper in the same pan for a minute.
Cook the spaghetti in the smallest amount of salted water that covers it.
Mash a third of the zucchini to a rough paste and return all of it to the pan with a ladle of pasta water.
Off the heat, toss the pasta through with both cheeses and the basil until glossy, loosening with more water as it thickens.

name: Spaghetti with garlic, chili and broccoli

ingredients.prep: cut into small florets, stalk peeled and sliced

steps: Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry pan until golden and tip them out.
Boil the broccoli in the pasta water for 4 minutes before the pasta goes in, then lift it out with a slotted spoon. Same pot, and the water is better for it.
Cook the spaghetti in that water.
Warm the garlic and chili flakes gently in the oil — pale gold, never brown — then add the broccoli and crush half of it against the pan so it becomes a sauce rather than a topping.
Toss the pasta through with a splash of its water, the parsley, lemon and crumbs.

name: Spaghetti with garlic, chili and chard
steps: Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry pan until golden and tip them out.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water.
Warm the garlic and chili flakes gently in the oil, then add the chard stalks and cook 4 minutes — they take about twice as long as the leaves, which is why they go in separately.
Add the leaves with a splash of pasta water and cook until collapsed.
Toss the pasta through, then finish with lemon, parmesan and the crumbs.

name: Spaghetti with garlic, chili and blistered tomatoes
steps: Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry pan until golden and tip them out.
Blister the tomatoes whole in a very hot dry pan until the skins split and char in places, then set aside. Leave them whole — the point is that each one bursts in the mouth.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water.
Warm the garlic and chili flakes gently in the oil until pale gold, then return the tomatoes and press half of them.
Toss the pasta through with a splash of its water, the basil and the crumbs.

name: Penne with artichokes, olives and capers
steps: Brown the artichoke quarters cut-side down in half the oil until they take colour, then lift them out. Jarred artichokes are already cooked; this is only about getting some edges on them.
Warm the garlic, chili flakes and oregano in the rest of the oil, then add the olives and capers for a minute.
Add the peppers and stock and simmer 12 minutes, crushing them against the pan into a sauce.
Cook the penne in well-salted water and drag it into the sauce with a splash of its water.
Fold the artichokes back through at the end so they stay in pieces. Taste before salting — olives and capers usually cover it.

name: Penne with roasted peppers, almonds and capers
steps: Warm the garlic, chili flakes and oregano in the oil until fragrant.
Add the olives, capers and peppers and cook 3 minutes.
Add the peppers and stock and simmer 12 minutes, crushing them as it goes, then blitz half the almonds in — they thicken it the way a romesco is thickened.
Cook the penne in well-salted water.
Drag the pasta into the sauce with a splash of its water and finish with parsley and pepper.

name: Zucchini carbonara
steps: Beat the eggs with the parmesan and a lot of black pepper.
Cook the pasta in well-salted water.
Fry the zucchini in the oil over high heat in two batches until browned at the edges, adding the garlic at the end. Two batches, or they steam.
Drain the pasta, keeping a mug of water, and add it to the zucchini pan off the heat.
Pour in the egg mixture and toss constantly, loosening with pasta water, until it coats. Off the heat throughout — this is a custard, not scrambled eggs. Finish with basil.

name: Pea and leek carbonara
steps: Beat the eggs with the parmesan and a lot of black pepper.
Soften the leeks in the butter and oil over low heat for 10 minutes, until sweet and collapsed. Low and slow — browned leeks are bitter in a sauce this plain.
Cook the pasta in well-salted water, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes.
Drain, keeping a mug of water, and tip the pasta and peas into the leek pan off the heat.
Pour in the egg mixture and toss constantly, loosening with pasta water, until it coats. Finish with mint.

name: Lentil and mushroom ragù bianco
steps: Brown the mushrooms hard in the oil in a wide pan, undisturbed at first, until the water has gone and the edges are dark. This is where the depth comes from and it cannot be hurried.
Add the onion and carrot and cook 8 minutes, then the garlic and thyme for a minute.
Add the stock, lentils and soy sauce. Simmer 25 minutes, until the lentils have gone soft enough to disappear into the sauce, then stir in the milk and give it 5 minutes more.
Cook the tagliatelle and drag it into the pan with a splash of its water.
Finish with parmesan, salt and pepper. Better still the next day.

name: Lentil and walnut ragù bianco
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan until they smell of themselves, then chop them fine.
Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 10 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 2 minutes more.
Add the stock, lentils and walnuts and simmer 25 minutes, then stir in the milk for the last 5.
The walnuts do the job the meat used to — fat and a slight coarseness — so keep them coarse enough to feel, not blitzed.
Cook the rigatoni, drag it into the sauce with a splash of its water, and finish with parmesan, salt and pepper.

name: Chard, butter bean and lemon pasta
steps: Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry pan until golden and set aside.
Cook the pasta, adding the chard stalks for the last 5 minutes and the leaves for the last 2.

Gently fry the garlic and chili flakes in the oil, then add the butter beans and crush about a third of them. Butter beans break down creamier than cannellini, so this is the version to make if you want a sauce rather than beans in a sauce.
Add the drained pasta and chard with a splash of the water and toss until creamy.
Finish with lemon juice, parmesan, the crumbs, salt and pepper.

name: Broccoli, white bean and lemon pasta
steps: Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry pan until golden and set aside.
Cook the pasta, adding the broccoli for the last 5 minutes so it goes soft enough to crush.
Gently fry the garlic and chili flakes in the oil, then add the beans and crush about a third of them.
Add the drained pasta and broccoli with a splash of the water, crushing some of the florets against the pan as you toss.
Finish with lemon juice, parmesan, the crumbs, salt and pepper.

name: Pasta e fagioli
steps: Soften the onion, celery and carrot in the oil for 10 minutes. Add the garlic and rosemary for a minute.
Add half the beans. Blitz or mash the other half with a ladle of stock and stir that in — it is what makes the broth creamy without any cream.
Pour in the rest of the stock, season, and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the ditalini and cook until just tender, stirring so it does not catch.
Rest 5 minutes off the heat, then finish with parmesan, pepper and a thread of oil. It should be thick enough to eat with a fork.

name: Pasta e lenticchie
steps: Soften the onion and celery in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, bay and chili flakes for a minute.
Add the lentils and stock and simmer 20 minutes, until the lentils are tender but still whole.
Add the ditalini and cook until just tender, stirring often — lentil starch and pasta starch together will stick to the bottom given any chance at all.
Fish out the bay leaves. Rest 5 minutes off the heat.
Finish with parsley, plenty of pepper and a thread of raw oil.

name: Eggplant and tomato pasta with ricotta salata
steps: Salt the eggplant cubes and leave 15 minutes, then pat dry. Fry them in the oil in batches until deep brown and collapsing.
Warm the garlic in the same pan, add the tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes.
Cook the penne in well-salted water.
Return the eggplant to the sauce and toss the drained pasta through with a splash of its water.

Grate the ricotta salata over at the table. It is salty and dry rather than creamy, which is the version Sicily actually makes — the soft ricotta in the parent recipe is the compromise for shops that do not stock it.

name: Eggplant and tomato pasta with smoked mozzarella
steps: Salt the eggplant cubes and leave 15 minutes, then pat dry. Fry them in the oil in batches until deep brown.
Warm the garlic in the same pan, add the tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes.
Cook the rigatoni in well-salted water and toss it through the sauce with the eggplant.
Stir the smoked mozzarella through off the heat so it softens into strands without releasing all its water.
Finish with basil, parmesan and pepper. Serve straight away — smoked mozzarella goes rubbery as it cools.

name: Roasted vegetable pasta with goat cheese
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the vegetables and unpeeled garlic with the oil, oregano, salt and pepper and roast 25-30 minutes, until the onion edges catch.
Cook the orzo in well-salted water and drain it while the tray is still hot.
Squeeze the roasted garlic out of its skins and mash it into the tray juices.
Tip the orzo onto the tray and stir everything together, scraping up the sticky bits.
Fold the goat cheese through while it is hot — unlike feta it melts into the juices and becomes the sauce. Finish with lemon.

name: Roasted vegetable pasta with halloumi
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the vegetables and unpeeled garlic with the oil, oregano and pepper and roast 20 minutes.
Scatter the halloumi over the tray and roast a further 10 minutes, until it is golden at the edges. Added at the start it goes hard; this is the window where it browns and still squeaks.
Cook the orzo in well-salted water — no extra salt in the tray, the halloumi brings plenty.
Squeeze the roasted garlic out of its skins and mash it into the tray juices, then stir the drained orzo through.
Finish with lemon and mint.

name: Lemon ricotta pasta with asparagus

ingredients.prep: woody ends snapped off, cut into short lengths

steps: Beat the ricotta with the lemon zest, oil, parmesan and plenty of pepper in the bottom of the serving bowl.
Cook the pasta in well-salted water, dropping the asparagus in for the last 3 minutes. Any longer and it goes khaki.
Loosen the ricotta with a few spoonfuls of the pasta water until it pours.
Tip the drained pasta and asparagus into the bowl and toss hard.
Finish with lemon juice and mint. Serve immediately — this sauce is only ever as good as it is hot.

name: Lemon ricotta pasta with edamame
steps: Beat the ricotta with the lemon zest, oil, parmesan, chili flakes and pepper in the bottom of the serving bowl.
Cook the pasta in well-salted water, adding the edamame for the last 3 minutes.
Loosen the ricotta with a few spoonfuls of the pasta water until it pours.
Tip the drained pasta and edamame in and toss hard. Crush a handful of the beans against the side of the bowl as you go.
Finish with lemon juice and mint. This is the version that eats like a meal rather than a starter — edamame carries about three times the protein of peas.

name: Pesto pasta with zucchini and potatoes
steps: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan and set aside.
Boil the potatoes in well-salted water for 5 minutes, then add the pasta.
Add the zucchini for the last 4 minutes. One pot, three things, timed backwards from when the pasta is done.
Drain, keeping a mug of the water, and stir the pesto through off the heat — pesto cooked in a hot pan turns grey and loses the basil.
Loosen with the water until it coats, then finish with parmesan, pine nuts and pepper.

name: Summer pasta primavera
steps: Cook the pasta in well-salted water.
Fry the corn in the oil over high heat until some kernels char, then add the zucchini and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the asparagus and cook just until it turns bright and squeaks — 3 minutes, no more.
Pour in the cream, let it bubble once, then toss the drained pasta through with a splash of its water.
Finish with lemon zest and juice, parmesan, green onions and basil.

name: Skillet lasagna with mushrooms
steps: Brown the mushrooms hard in the oil in a wide ovenproof pan until the edges are dark, then add the onion and cook 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and thyme for a minute, then the passata and a mug of water.
Slide the broken sheets in one at a time so they do not weld together, pushing them under the sauce. Simmer 15 minutes, stirring gently.
Dot the ricotta and mozzarella over the top and put it under a hot grill for 5 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes before serving — straight out of the pan it is soup, and five minutes later it is lasagna.

name: Skillet lasagna with butternut and sage
steps: Fry the sage leaves in the oil until crisp and lift them out.
Brown the squash in the same pan for 8 minutes, then add the onion and cook 6 more.
Add the garlic, nutmeg, stock and cream. Keep it on the loose side — the squash drinks more liquid than you expect as it softens.
Slide the broken sheets in one at a time, push them under, and simmer 15 minutes.
Dot with ricotta and mozzarella, grill 5 minutes, then rest 5 and scatter the fried sage over.

name: Gnocchi with peas and lemon
steps: Boil the gnocchi until they float, adding the peas for the last minute. Keep a mug of the water.
Melt the butter in a wide pan and let it foam, then add the lemon zest.
Tip the drained gnocchi and peas in with a splash of the water and toss until the sauce clings.
Crush a spoonful of the peas against the pan — it thickens the butter into something that coats rather than pools.
Finish with lemon juice, parmesan, mint and plenty of pepper.

name: Gnocchi with chard and brown butter
steps: Boil the chard stalks for 3 minutes in the water the gnocchi will use, then lift them out.
Cook the gnocchi until they float, adding the chard leaves for the last 30 seconds.

Brown the butter with the walnuts and garlic until it smells nutty and the solids are the colour of a hazelnut. This happens fast and then it burns, so take it off while you still think it could go further.
Add the chili flakes, stalks and leaves, then the drained gnocchi and a splash of the water.
Finish with lemon, parmesan, salt and pepper.

name: Baked gnocchi with spinach and ricotta
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C.
Warm the garlic and oregano in the oil in an ovenproof pan, add the passata and simmer 5 minutes.
Wilt the spinach into the sauce a handful at a time, then season with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Stir the gnocchi in raw — they cook in the sauce, which is the whole point of the dish and also why the sauce has to be loose enough to boil.
Dot with ricotta and mozzarella, scatter the parmesan, and bake 20 minutes until blistered.

name: Cauliflower mac and cheese
steps: Cook the macaroni in well-salted water, adding the cauliflower for the last 6 minutes so it goes soft at the edges.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then add the milk a little at a time, whisking, until smooth and thick.
Take it off the heat before the cheese goes in, with the mustard, nutmeg, salt and pepper. Cheese boiled in a sauce splits.
Fold the drained macaroni and cauliflower through, crushing a few florets so they thicken the sauce.
Top with the breadcrumbs and grill 5 minutes until brown.

name: Three-cheese mac
steps: Cook the cavatappi in well-salted water — corkscrews hold three times the sauce a straight tube does, which is the reason for them here.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then whisk in the milk a little at a time until smooth and thick.
Off the heat, add the cheddar for salt, the gruyère for the stretch and the parmesan for the savoury edge, with the mustard, nutmeg and pepper.
Fold the drained pasta through and taste for salt — three cheeses vary, so this one genuinely needs tasting.
Top with the breadcrumbs and grill 5 minutes.

name: Chickpea minestrone
steps: Soften the onion, carrot, celery and fennel in the oil for 12 minutes. This is the whole flavour of the soup, so give it the time.
Add the garlic and rosemary for a minute, then the stock.
Add the chickpeas, crushing a third of them against the side of the pot, and simmer 12 minutes.
Add the ditalini and kale and cook until the pasta is just tender.
Finish with parmesan, pepper and a thread of raw oil. Thickens overnight; loosen with water when you reheat it.

name: Peanut noodles with edamame
steps: Whisk the peanut butter, soy, vinegar, honey, sesame oil, ginger, garlic and sriracha with 100ml warm water until it pours.
Soak or boil the rice noodles as the packet says, adding the edamame for the last 2 minutes, then rinse both under cold water to stop them gluing together.
Toss the noodles and edamame through the sauce.
No frying at all in this version — the beans arrive cooked and the protein comes free, which makes it the fastest thing in the family.
Top with the carrot, cucumber, green onions and cilantro.

name: Peanut noodles with broccoli and tofu
steps: Press the tofu for 10 minutes, cube it, and fry in the oil until golden on several sides.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy, vinegar, honey, sesame oil, ginger, garlic and sriracha with 100ml warm water.
Cook the noodles as the packet says, dropping the broccoli in for the last 3 minutes, then rinse under cold water.
Toss everything through the sauce while the tofu is still hot.
Finish with green onions and crushed peanuts.

name: Tofu lo mein
steps: Press the tofu 10 minutes and cut it into batons. Batons rather than cubes, so it reads as a noodle rather than as something dropped into noodles.
Whisk the soy, hoisin, sesame oil, vinegar and cornstarch with 100ml water.
Fry the tofu in the oil until crisp on two sides and set aside.
Cook the noodles, rinse, and drain well.
Stir-fry the ginger and garlic for 30 seconds, add the cabbage, carrots and snap peas for 3 minutes, then the noodles, tofu and sauce. Toss until it clings. Finish with green onions.

name: Bok choy and chili lo mein
steps: Whisk the soy, hoisin, sesame oil, vinegar and cornstarch with 100ml water.
Cook the noodles, rinse under cold water and drain well. Wet noodles steam instead of frying and the sauce slides off them.
Brown the mushrooms hard in the oil, then add the ginger, garlic, fresh chili and chili flakes for 30 seconds.
Add the bok choy cut-side down and leave it alone for 2 minutes to take colour, then the carrot.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss over high heat until it clings. Finish with green onions.

name: Kimchi yaki udon
steps: Whisk the soy, mirin, gochujang and vinegar together.
Fry the kimchi in the oil over high heat for 2 minutes until it darkens and smells sweet rather than sharp. Frying it is what separates this from noodles with kimchi on top.
Add the cabbage and carrot for 2 minutes, then the udon and the sauce, tossing until everything is coated.
Fry the eggs separately, keeping the yolks soft.
Serve with an egg on each bowl, the green onions, sesame oil and sesame seeds.

name: Tofu and bok choy yaki udon
steps: Press the tofu 10 minutes, cube it and fry in the oil until golden on several sides. Take it out of the pan before anything else goes in.
Whisk the soy, mirin, hoisin and vinegar.
Fry the shiitake hard until the edges crisp, then add the carrot and bok choy stems for 2 minutes.
Add the udon, the leaves, the tofu and the sauce and toss over high heat until glossy.
Finish with sesame oil, green onions and nori torn over.

name: Japchae with tofu
steps: Press the tofu 10 minutes, cut into batons and fry in the oil until golden.
Cook the glass noodles for 6 minutes, rinse, drain and cut through them a few times with scissors.

Cook each vegetable separately in the same pan — onion, then pepper, then carrot, then mushrooms — a minute or two each. Cooked together they stew; cooked apart they stay distinct, which is what japchae is.
Wilt the spinach last and squeeze it dry.
Toss everything with the soy, sesame oil, sugar and garlic, then the tofu. Finish with sesame seeds and green onions. Good warm or at room temperature.

name: Dan dan style noodles with tofu
steps: Crumble the tofu with your hands and fry it in the oil, undisturbed at first, until the curds are brown and dry at the edges — 8 minutes or so. Dry is the goal; wet tofu will not hold seasoning.
Season the tofu with a tablespoon of the soy and half the chili flakes.
Whisk the tahini, remaining soy, vinegar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, sugar and the rest of the chili with 100ml warm water.
Cook the noodles, blanching the bok choy in the same water for the last minute.
Pool the sauce in the bowls, pile the noodles on, then the tofu, peanuts and green onions. Stir it all together at the table.

name: Pad thai style noodles with tempeh
steps: Steam or simmer the tempeh cubes for 5 minutes first — it takes the bitter edge off, and it is the step everybody skips.
Whisk the tamarind, soy, sugar and chili flakes into a sauce.
Fry the tempeh in the oil until dark gold on all sides, then push it aside and scramble the eggs in the same pan.
Soak the noodles until pliable but not soft, then add them with the sauce and garlic and toss over high heat for 2 minutes.
Fold in the bean sprouts and green onions off the heat. Serve with peanuts, cilantro and lime.

name: Sopa de fideo with black beans
steps: Fry the broken spaghetti in the oil, stirring constantly, until it is the colour of straw. Toasting the pasta first is the whole dish; skip it and this is just soup with noodles in.
Blend the roasted peppers, onion, garlic, cumin and chili powder smooth and pour it into the pan — it will spit.
Cook 5 minutes until it darkens, then add the stock and the beans.
Simmer 10 minutes until the pasta is soft. It should stay soupy; it will drink more liquid as it stands.
Serve with avocado, queso fresco, cilantro and a hard squeeze of lime.

name: Mushroom laksa
steps: Brown both mushrooms hard in the oil until the edges are dark and the pan is dry. Mushrooms in a coconut broth go slippery unless they are browned first.
Push them aside, add the curry paste and fry 2 minutes until it smells toasted and the oil splits out.
Add the coconut milk and stock, the soy and the sugar, and simmer 10 minutes.
Cook the noodles separately and divide them between bowls — noodles left in the broth swell and drink it.
Blanch the bok choy in the broth, then ladle over the noodles. Top with bean sprouts, cilantro, chili and lime.

name: Soba noodle salad with avocado
steps: Cook the soba, then rinse under cold water rubbing the strands between your hands until they squeak. Soba left unrinsed goes claggy within minutes.
Whisk the soy, vinegar, mirin and sesame oil.
Toss the noodles through the dressing.
Add the avocado at the last moment with a squeeze of lime over it.
Top with radish, cucumber, green onions, sesame seeds and torn nori.

name: Cold peanut noodle salad
steps: Whisk the peanut butter, soy, vinegar, sesame oil, honey, lime and chili flakes with 3 tablespoons of warm water until smooth and pourable.
Cook the noodles, adding the edamame for the last 2 minutes, then rinse cold.
Toss everything through the sauce.
Peanut butter thickens as it sits, so if this is going in a box, keep a spoonful of the sauce back and loosen it in the morning.
Top with the vegetables and crushed peanuts.

name: Käsespätzle with mushrooms
steps: Fry the onions slowly in half the butter for 20 minutes until deep brown and sweet. Start them before anything else.
Beat the flour, eggs, milk, nutmeg, salt and pepper to a thick batter and rest it 10 minutes.
Brown the mushrooms with the thyme in the oil and the rest of the butter.
Press the batter through a colander into boiling salted water; the spätzle are done when they float, about 2 minutes.
Layer the spätzle with both cheeses and the mushrooms in a warm dish so the cheese melts between the layers, then pile the onions and chives on top.

name: Miso noodle soup with mushrooms
steps: Put the kombu and shiitake in 1.2 litres of cold water and bring it slowly to just below a simmer, then lift the kombu out. Boiled kombu turns the broth bitter.
Simmer 10 minutes, then add the cremini, soy, mirin and ginger for 5 minutes more.
Cook the udon separately and divide between bowls.
Off the heat, whisk the miso with a ladle of broth and stir it back in. Miso boiled loses its smell and half its point.
Wilt the spinach in the hot broth, ladle over the noodles, and finish with green onions, sesame oil and seeds.

name: Sticky tempeh noodles with greens
steps: Steam the tempeh slices 5 minutes, then pat dry.
Whisk the soy, maple, vinegar and sriracha.
Fry the tempeh in the oil until dark on both sides, pour half the sauce over and let it reduce to a glaze. Take it out before it catches — maple burns quickly.
Stir-fry the broccoli with a splash of water, lid on for 2 minutes, then the kale, ginger and garlic.
Add the cooked noodles and the rest of the sauce, toss, and return the tempeh. Finish with sesame oil, seeds and green onions.

name: Creamy tomato rigatoni
steps: Soften the onion in the butter and oil for 8 minutes without colouring.

Add the garlic and chili flakes, then the tomato paste, and fry it for a full 4 minutes until it darkens to brick red and sticks to the pan. This step is the difference between a sauce that tastes cooked and one that tastes of the tin.
Pour in the cream and 200ml of water and simmer 5 minutes.
Cook the rigatoni a minute short and finish it in the sauce with a ladle of its water.
Off the heat, stir in the parmesan and basil. Season and serve at once.

name: Creamy tomato rigatoni with mascarpone
steps: Soften the onion in the butter and oil for 8 minutes without colouring.
Add the garlic and chili flakes, then the tomato paste, and fry it 4 minutes until it darkens and sticks.
Loosen with 300ml of water and simmer 5 minutes.
Cook the rigatoni a minute short, then finish it in the sauce with a ladle of its water.
Stir the mascarpone in off the heat. It is thicker than cream and does not need reducing, so it goes in last and the sauce is ready the moment it melts. Finish with parmesan and basil.

name: Creamy tomato and roasted pepper rigatoni
steps: Soften the onion in the butter and oil for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, paprika and chili flakes, then the tomato paste, and fry 3 minutes until it darkens.
Blend the peppers smooth and add them with the cream. Simmer 8 minutes — jarred peppers are watery and the sauce needs that time to tighten.
Cook the rigatoni a minute short and finish it in the sauce with a ladle of its water.
Off the heat, stir in the parmesan and basil, then season.

name: Orecchiette with broccoli and chili

ingredients.prep: cut into small florets, stalk peeled and sliced

steps: Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry pan until golden and tip them out.
Boil the broccoli in well-salted water for 6 minutes, until softer than you would normally want it, then scoop it out. Cook the orecchiette in the same water.
Warm the garlic and chili flakes gently in the oil, add the broccoli and crush it to a rough sauce with the back of a spoon.
Drag the pasta across with a ladle of its water and toss hard so the sauce lodges in the cups. Ear-shaped pasta is the point: each one carries a spoonful.
Finish with pecorino, lemon, the crumbs and pepper.

name: Orecchiette with cavolo nero
steps: Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry pan until golden and tip them out.
Boil the kale in well-salted water for 5 minutes, then scoop it out and cook the orecchiette in the same water.
Warm the garlic and chili flakes in the oil, add the kale and the beans, and crush about half of both to a rough paste.
Drag the pasta across with a ladle of its water and toss until it coats.
Finish with pecorino, lemon, the crumbs and pepper.

name: Orecchiette with broccoli rabe

ingredients.prep: trimmed and cut into short lengths

steps: Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry pan until golden and tip them out.
Boil the broccoli rabe in well-salted water for 3 minutes and scoop it out. The blanching water carries off some of the bitterness, which is why this one is not simply fried from raw.
Cook the orecchiette in the same water.
Warm the garlic and chili flakes in the oil, add the rabe and cook 3 minutes, crushing some of it against the pan.
Toss the pasta through with a ladle of its water, then finish with pecorino, lemon, the crumbs and pepper. This is the original the other two are standing in for.

name: Baked rigatoni al forno
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, add the garlic, oregano and chili flakes, then the passata. Simmer 10 minutes.
Boil the rigatoni for half the time on the packet. It finishes in the oven, and pasta cooked through twice turns to paste.
Toss the drained pasta with the sauce and a mug of the pasta water — it looks too wet, and it should; the tubes drink it as they bake.
Layer into a dish with the mozzarella, top with parmesan and bake 20 minutes until blistered. Scatter the basil over at the table.

name: Baked rigatoni with spinach and ricotta
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Soften the onion in the oil, add the garlic and oregano, then the passata, and simmer 10 minutes.
Wilt the spinach, squeeze it hard in a tea towel, chop it, and beat it into the ricotta with the nutmeg, salt and pepper. Squeezing is not optional — spinach water will thin the whole dish.
Boil the rigatoni for half the packet time and toss with the sauce and a mug of pasta water.
Layer with spoonfuls of the ricotta mixture and the mozzarella, top with parmesan, and bake 20 minutes.

name: Baked rigatoni with eggplant
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Toss the eggplant with 3 tablespoons of the oil and a teaspoon of salt and roast 25 minutes until collapsing.
Meanwhile warm the garlic, oregano and chili flakes in the rest of the oil, add the passata and simmer 10 minutes.
Boil the rigatoni for half the packet time.
Fold the pasta, sauce, roasted eggplant and a mug of pasta water together.
Layer with the mozzarella, top with parmesan and bake 15 minutes. Basil at the table.

name: Pasta with walnut sauce
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 5 minutes, then rub them in a cloth to shed the loose skins. The skins are where the bitterness lives.
Soak the bread in the milk.
Blend the walnuts, soaked bread, garlic, parmesan, oil and nutmeg to a thick cream, loosening with pasta water.
This sauce is never cooked — it is a Ligurian salsa, and heating it makes it grainy. Warm the bowl instead.
Cook the tagliatelle, toss it through the sauce with plenty of its water, and finish with parsley and pepper.

name: Pasta with walnut and ricotta sauce
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 5 minutes and rub off the loose skins.
Blend them with the ricotta, garlic, parmesan, oil, lemon zest and nutmeg until almost smooth. Ricotta replaces the soaked bread, which makes this one lighter and rather quicker.
Warm the serving bowl — this sauce is not cooked.
Cook the tagliatelle and toss it through with a good ladle of its water until it pours.
Finish with lemon juice, parsley, salt and pepper.

name: Pappardelle with mushroom ragù
steps: Chop the mushrooms by hand to the size of peas — a food processor turns them to slurry and the ragù loses its texture.
Brown them hard in half the oil in two batches, leaving each batch alone until the water has gone and the edges are dark.
Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the rest of the oil for 12 minutes, then add the garlic, thyme and bay.
Return the mushrooms with the stock and soy, and simmer 20 minutes until glossy and thick.
Cook the pappardelle and finish it in the pan with a splash of its water. Parmesan and pepper at the table.

name: Pappardelle with porcini ragù
steps: Soak the porcini in 300ml of just-boiled water for 20 minutes. Lift them out, chop them, and keep the liquid — pour it off carefully and leave the grit in the bottom of the cup. That liquid is the reason to make this version.
Brown the cremini hard in half the oil in two batches.
Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the rest of the oil for 12 minutes, then add the garlic, thyme and bay.
Return all the mushrooms with the stock and the porcini liquor and simmer 20 minutes, then stir the cream through.
Stir the cream through at the end, cook the pappardelle, and finish it in the pan with a splash of its water.

name: Pappardelle with mushroom and lentil ragù
steps: Brown the mushrooms hard in half the oil in two batches until the edges are dark.
Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the rest of the oil for 12 minutes, then add the garlic, thyme, bay and miso for 2 minutes.
Add the lentils and stock and simmer 25 minutes, until the lentils are tender and holding their shape. Brown lentils rather than red, because this ragù wants something to bite on.
Return the mushrooms and cook 5 minutes more; it should be thick, not soupy.
Cook the pappardelle and finish it in the pan with a splash of its water. Freezes well.

name: Fusilli with roasted pepper sauce
steps: Warm the garlic, paprika and chili flakes in the oil until fragrant but not coloured.
Blend the peppers with the garlic oil until smooth, then return it to the pan and cook 8 minutes, until it darkens and stops tasting of the jar.
Cook the fusilli in well-salted water. Spirals hold a smooth sauce better than tubes do, which is the whole reason for the shape here.
Toss the pasta through with a ladle of its water and the parmesan.
Finish with lemon, parsley, salt and pepper.

name: Fusilli with pepper and almond sauce
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan until they colour, then set a few aside to chop for the top.
Blend the rest with the peppers, raw garlic, oil, paprika, vinegar and chili flakes to a coarse romesco — coarse, not smooth; the grit of the nuts is the texture of the dish.
Warm it gently in a pan for 5 minutes. It does not need long, and boiling makes it split.
Cook the fusilli and toss it through with a ladle of its water.
Finish with the chopped almonds, parsley, parmesan and pepper.

name: One-pot tomato and basil pasta
steps: Put the linguine, tomatoes, onion, garlic, chili flakes, oil, salt and half the basil in a wide pan with 900ml of cold water.
Bring to the boil and cook 10-12 minutes, turning the pasta constantly with tongs. The turning is the whole technique: it is what stops the strands welding and what pulls the starch out into a sauce.
When the water has almost gone the sauce should cling. If it goes dry too early, add a splash more.
Off the heat, stir through the parmesan and the rest of the basil.
One pan, no colander, and the starch you would normally pour away is the sauce.

name: One-pot tomato and spinach pasta
steps: Put the linguine, tomatoes, onion, garlic, chili flakes, oil and salt in a wide pan with 900ml of cold water.
Bring to the boil and cook 10-12 minutes, turning constantly with tongs.
Pile the spinach on top for the last 2 minutes and fold it through as it collapses.
Off the heat, stir through the parmesan and lemon zest.
Season and serve straight from the pan.

name: One-pot tomato pasta with mozzarella
steps: Put the linguine, tomatoes, onion, garlic, oregano, chili flakes, oil and salt in a wide pan with 900ml of cold water.
Bring to the boil and cook 10-12 minutes, turning constantly with tongs.
Take the pan off the heat and scatter the mozzarella over. Put a lid on for 2 minutes and leave it alone — stirring it in turns the sauce stringy and grey.
Fold it through once, roughly, so there are still molten pockets.
Finish with basil and pepper.

name: Baked feta and tomato pasta
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Put the tomatoes and unpeeled garlic in a baking dish, sit the feta in the middle, pour the oil over and scatter the oregano and chili flakes.
Bake 35 minutes, until the tomatoes have burst and the feta is soft and browning at the edges.
Cook the fusilli in well-salted water in the last 12 minutes.
Squeeze the garlic out of its skins, then mash everything in the dish together into a sauce.
Fold the drained pasta through with a splash of its water, then the basil and lemon. No salt — the feta brings all of it.

name: Baked feta pasta with harissa and peppers
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Put the peppers and unpeeled garlic in a dish, sit the feta in the middle, and spoon the harissa and oil over with the cumin.
Bake 35 minutes, until the peppers have caught at the edges and the harissa has gone dark around the dish.
Cook the fusilli in well-salted water in the last 12 minutes.
Squeeze the garlic out of its skins and mash the dish together.
Fold the pasta through with a splash of its water, then the cilantro and lemon. Harissa varies wildly in heat, so taste before you decide whether it needs the second spoonful.

name: Baked goat cheese and tomato pasta
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Put the tomatoes and unpeeled garlic in a dish with the oil, thyme, chili flakes and salt.
Bake 20 minutes, then sit the goat cheese in the middle, trickle the honey over it and bake 12 minutes more. Goat cheese is wetter than feta and goes grainy over a long bake, so it goes in late.
Cook the fusilli in well-salted water.
Squeeze out the garlic and mash the dish together into a sauce.
Fold the pasta through with a splash of its water and finish with basil and pepper.

name: Spinach and ricotta stuffed shells
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Boil the shells for 3 minutes less than the packet says and lay them out separately so they do not stick.
Wilt the spinach, squeeze it bone dry in a tea towel and chop it. Wet spinach is the one thing that ruins this.
Beat it into the ricotta with the egg, half the parmesan, the nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Warm the garlic in the oil, add the passata and simmer 5 minutes, then spread it in a dish.
Fill the shells, sit them in the sauce, top with mozzarella and the rest of the parmesan, and bake 30 minutes. Basil at the table. Assembles a day ahead and bakes from cold in 45.

name: Butternut and ricotta stuffed shells
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Roast the squash with a tablespoon of the oil for 25 minutes, then mash it roughly and let it cool a little.
Boil the shells 3 minutes short and lay them out separately.
Beat the squash into the ricotta with the egg, half the parmesan, the chopped sage, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Warm the garlic in the rest of the oil, add the passata, simmer 5 minutes and spread it in a dish.
Fill the shells, top with mozzarella and parmesan, and bake 30 minutes at 190°C.

name: Butternut squash and sage pasta
steps: Fry the sage leaves in the butter and oil until crisp, then lift them out on to paper.
Cook the squash and onion in the same pan for 15 minutes, lid on, until collapsing, then add the garlic and chili flakes.
Add the stock and blend about half of it — half blended is the trick, so it is a sauce with pieces in rather than a soup.
Cook the farfalle and fold it through with a splash of its water and the parmesan.
Crumble the fried sage over. Season well; squash needs more salt than seems reasonable.

name: Butternut and blue cheese pasta
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan and set aside.
Cook the squash and onion in the butter and oil for 15 minutes, lid on, with the thyme, then add the garlic.
Add the stock and blend half of it.
Cook the farfalle and fold it through with a splash of its water, then stir in two thirds of the blue cheese off the heat.
Scatter the rest of the cheese and the walnuts over. No added salt — blue cheese carries plenty, and how much depends entirely on which one you bought.

name: Butternut pasta with walnuts and chili
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan, then chop half of them fine and leave the rest in pieces.
Cook the squash and onion in the oil for 15 minutes, lid on, then add the garlic and chili flakes.
Add the stock and the finely chopped walnuts and blend half the pan — the ground nuts give the sauce body without any dairy in it.
Cook the farfalle and fold it through with a splash of its water.
Top with spoonfuls of ricotta, the remaining walnuts, lemon zest and parsley.

name: Summer pasta salad
steps: Cook the farfalle, drain, and toss it with the oil while still hot. Hot pasta drinks dressing; cold pasta wears it.
Soak the sliced onion in the vinegar for 10 minutes to take the raw edge off, then whisk in the mustard and pour the lot over the pasta.
Add the pepper and cucumber and leave 15 minutes for the dressing to soak in.
Fold in the mozzarella and basil just before serving.
Keeps two days; add the basil fresh each time.

name: Greek pasta salad
steps: Cook the farfalle, drain, and toss it with the oil while still hot.
Soak the onion in the vinegar and lemon juice for 10 minutes, then pour it over the pasta with the oregano.
Add the pepper, cucumber and olives and leave 15 minutes.
Fold the feta through at the end so the cubes stay whole.
No salt: between the feta and the olives there is plenty. Pepper, though.

name: Pesto pasta salad
steps: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan and set aside.
Cook the farfalle, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes, then drain and rinse briefly under cold water.
Stir the pesto through with the oil and lemon juice while the pasta is warm but not hot — pesto in a hot pan goes grey.
Fold in the snap peas and arugula just before serving so the leaves do not wilt in the box.
Finish with parmesan, pine nuts and pepper.

name: Tortellini in brodo
steps: Simmer the stock with the carrot, celery, leek and bay for 15 minutes, then fish out the vegetables and the bay. A brodo is about the broth, and the vegetables have done their work by then.
Bring it back to a bare simmer — a rolling boil splits tortellini open.
Drop the tortellini in and cook 3-4 minutes, until they float and swell.
Ladle into warm bowls with plenty of the broth.
Parmesan and pepper over the top, and nothing else. This is deliberately thin — it is a broth with something in it, not a soup.

name: Tortellini in brodo with peas
steps: Simmer the stock with the carrot and leek for 15 minutes, then lift them out.
Bring it back to a bare simmer — a rolling boil splits tortellini.
Drop the tortellini in for 3-4 minutes, adding the peas for the last 2 and the spinach for the last 30 seconds.
Ladle into warm bowls and finish with lemon zest, mint and parmesan.
Pepper over the top. Still thin, still a broth — the peas are there for sweetness, not body.

name: Fregola with tomatoes and chickpeas
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes with the fennel seeds and chili flakes, then add the garlic.
Add the tomatoes and cook until they collapse, 8 minutes.
Stir in the fregola and toast it for a minute — it is toasted semolina to begin with, and a minute in the pan brings that back.
Add the chickpeas and stock and simmer 12 minutes, stirring, until the fregola is tender and the pan is creamy rather than soupy.
Finish with lemon zest and juice, parsley, pecorino and pepper.

name: Fregola with saffron and fennel
steps: Steep the saffron in 3 tablespoons of hot stock while you start the vegetables. Saffron gives nothing to a dry pan.
Soften the onion and fennel in the oil for 12 minutes, until sweet, then add the garlic.
Toast the fregola in the pan for a minute.
Add the chickpeas, stock and the saffron with its liquid, and simmer 12 minutes until creamy.
Finish with lemon, parsley, pecorino and pepper.

name: Ash reshteh
steps: Fry the sliced onions in the oil over medium heat for 20 minutes until deep brown, then lift out half for the top and add the garlic and turmeric to the rest.
Add the lentils and stock and simmer 20 minutes, then the beans and chickpeas.
Add all the herbs and the spinach — an enormous amount, and they collapse to almost nothing. The soup should turn green.
Stir in the broken noodles and cook 10 minutes, stirring often; they thicken the pot as much as they fill it.
Serve with the reserved onions, the sour cream swirled in, and the mint crushed between your fingers over the top.

name: Ash reshteh with beets
steps: Fry the sliced onions in the oil for 20 minutes until deep brown, reserving half, then add the garlic and turmeric.
Add the beets, lentils and stock and simmer 25 minutes until the beets are tender.
Add the chickpeas, all the herbs and the spinach.
Stir in the broken noodles and cook 10 minutes, stirring often.
Finish with lemon juice, which the beets need, then the reserved onions and the sour cream. It comes out magenta and that is correct.

name: Rishta — lentil and noodle soup
steps: Fry the onions in half the oil for 20 minutes until deeply browned and sweet. Keep a third of them back for the top.
Add the lentils and stock and simmer 20 minutes.

Make the taqliya: fry the crushed garlic with the ground coriander and most of the cilantro in the rest of the oil for a minute, until it smells green and sharp, then tip the lot into the pot. Adding garlic and coriander this late rather than at the start is the entire character of the soup.
Add the broken noodles and cook 10 minutes.
Finish with lemon juice, the reserved onions and the last of the cilantro.

name: Harira with broken noodles
steps: Soften the onion and celery in the oil for 10 minutes, then add the ginger, turmeric and cinnamon for a minute.
Add the stock and cook 10 minutes, letting the onion and celery soften right down into it.
Add the lentils, chickpeas and stock and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the broken spaghetti and half the herbs and cook 10 minutes more. It should be thick — harira is closer to a stew than a broth.
Finish with lemon juice and the rest of the herbs, and check the salt: it takes more than you expect.

name: Scallion oil noodles

ingredients.prep: cut into lengths, white and green kept apart

steps: Put the green onion whites in the cold oil in a cold pan, then bring it up slowly over low heat. Starting cold is the whole method: the onions dry out and candy rather than frying and burning.
After 10 minutes add the green parts and cook another 8, until everything is dark brown and crisp and the oil smells sweet.
Lift the onions out. Stir the soy, sugar and vinegar into the oil and let it bubble for 30 seconds.
Cook the noodles and toss them straight into the pan with the sauce.
Pile the crisp onions back on top with the sesame oil. Four ingredients, twenty minutes, and better than it has any right to be.

name: Chili scallion oil noodles
steps: Put the green onions in the cold oil and bring it up slowly over low heat for 18 minutes, until dark and crisp. Lift them out.
Put the chili flakes, garlic and sesame seeds in a heatproof bowl.
Pour the hot oil over them — it should sizzle hard and settle. If it does not sizzle the oil was too cool, and if it smells scorched it was too hot.
Stir in the soy, sugar and vinegar.
Cook the noodles, toss them through, and top with the crisp onions and sesame oil.

name: Skillet pastitsio
steps: Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 20 minutes until soft, then drain.

Soften the onion in the oil, add the garlic, cinnamon and allspice, then the peppers, stock and lentils. Cook 10 minutes to a thick ragù. The cinnamon is what makes this Greek rather than Italian, so do not be shy with it.
Make a béchamel: melt the butter, stir in the flour, cook 2 minutes, then whisk in the milk until thick. Off the heat beat in the eggs and half the parmesan.
Cook the penne 3 minutes short, fold it through the ragù and level it in an ovenproof pan.
Pour the béchamel over, scatter the rest of the parmesan, and bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until set and brown. Rest 10 minutes or it will not slice.

name: Pasta with garlic yogurt and chili butter

ingredients.prep: crushed to a paste with salt

steps: Take the yogurt out of the fridge before you start. Beat it with the garlic paste and a pinch of salt and leave it to come to room temperature — fridge-cold yogurt under hot pasta splits every time.
Cook the farfalle in well-salted water.
Melt the butter with the chili flakes and paprika until it foams and turns red, then add the walnuts for 30 seconds.
Spread the garlic yogurt over a warm platter, pile the drained pasta on, and spoon the chili butter over the top.
Mint and pepper to finish. Eat immediately, tossing it together on the plate.

name: Pancit bihon
steps: Soak the rice noodles in warm water for 10 minutes until pliable, then drain.
Fry the tofu in the oil until golden and set aside.
Fry the onion and garlic, then the carrots and beans for 3 minutes, then the cabbage for 2.

Pour in the stock and soy, bring to a simmer, then add the drained noodles and toss until they have drunk nearly all of it — 4 minutes or so. Cooking them in the stock rather than in water is what makes this pancit and not a stir-fry.
Return the tofu, finish with green onions and plenty of pepper, and serve with lime wedges to squeeze over.

name: Curried rice noodles
steps: Soak the rice vermicelli in warm water until pliable, then drain well.
Fry the tofu batons in half the oil until golden and set aside, then scramble the eggs in the same pan and set those aside too.
Fry the curry powder and turmeric in the rest of the oil for 30 seconds — a dry spice needs oil and heat to stop tasting of dust, and this is the step that decides the dish.
Add the onion, pepper and garlic for 3 minutes, then the noodles, soy and vinegar, tossing with tongs until evenly yellow.
Fold in the sprouts, egg, tofu and green onions, and finish with sesame oil.

name: Drunken noodles with tofu
steps: Soak the wide rice noodles until just pliable — they finish in the pan, and fully soft noodles break up under tossing.
