Whisk the soy, hoisin and sugar together.
Fry the tofu in the oil over the highest heat you have until browned, then add the garlic and chilies for 20 seconds.

Add the beans and peppers for 2 minutes, then the noodles and sauce, tossing hard and leaving them still for a few seconds at a time so they catch and char in places. That char is the point of the dish.
Off the heat, fold in a huge handful of basil and squeeze the lime over.

name: Fideuà
steps: Toast the broken spaghetti in 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wide shallow pan until golden, then tip it out. This is fideuà rather than paella and the toasting is the whole reason it works.
Steep the saffron in a little warm stock.
Soften the onion and pepper in the rest of the oil for 8 minutes, then the garlic and paprika, then the roasted peppers. Cook until jammy, 5 minutes.
Return the pasta, add the stock and saffron, and spread it flat. Do not stir again — a crust on the bottom is wanted. Simmer 12 minutes, adding the beans and artichokes after 5.
Rest 5 minutes off the heat. Stir the lemon juice and a crushed garlic clove into the mayonnaise and serve it alongside, with parsley over the top.

name: Mushroom giouvetsi
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Brown the mushrooms hard in the oil in an ovenproof dish until the edges darken.
Add the onion for 6 minutes, then the garlic, cinnamon, allspice and oregano.
Add the peppers and cook 5 minutes, then the orzo and the stock.
Bake uncovered 25 minutes, stirring once at the halfway mark so the orzo on top does not dry to gravel.
Crumble the feta over and bake 5 minutes more. Rest 5 minutes — it thickens as it sits — then finish with parsley and pepper.

name: Yōshoku soy butter spaghetti
steps: Cook the spaghetti two minutes past al dente, drain, toss with a little oil and leave it 10 minutes. Soft, rested noodles are not a mistake here — this is a post-war Japanese diner dish and the texture is the whole nostalgia of it.
Fry the onion, pepper and mushrooms in the butter and oil until soft.
Add the hoisin, paprika, sugar and soy and fry 3 minutes until it darkens and clings to the vegetables.
Add the spaghetti and toss over medium heat until every strand is orange and slightly sticky.
Parmesan and plenty of pepper at the table.

name: Tallarines verdes
steps: Boil the potato wedges until tender and keep them warm — in Peru this arrives with something starchy alongside the pasta, which sounds like too much and is not.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil, then blend them with the spinach, basil, walnuts, queso fresco and milk until smooth and bright green.
Cook the spaghetti.
Warm the sauce gently in the pan — gently, because boiling turns it army green — and toss the pasta through with a splash of its water.
Season and serve with the potatoes, and more cheese crumbled over.

name: Lemon and orzo soup
steps: Soften the carrot and celery in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the stock and bring to a simmer.
Add the orzo and cook 9 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the lemon juice, then temper: ladle hot broth into the eggs a little at a time, whisking constantly, until the bowl is warm. Rushing this scrambles them and there is no way back.
Pour the tempered mixture into the pot off the heat and stir until it thickens to the texture of thin cream. Do not let it boil again.
Finish with dill, salt and pepper. Thickens considerably as it stands; loosen with hot stock.

name: Pastina in brodo
steps: Bring the stock to a simmer and cook the pastina in it — in it, not in water. The starch is what turns a broth into this.
Beat the egg with half the parmesan and a little lemon zest.
Off the heat, pour it in in a thin stream while stirring so it sets in threads rather than lumps.
Stir in the butter and the rest of the parmesan.
Plenty of pepper. Eat from a mug if the day calls for it.

name: Sweet noodle kugel
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and butter a dish well.
Boil the noodles until just tender and drain — they carry on cooking in the custard, so stop early.
Soak the raisins in hot water for 10 minutes and drain; dry ones burn on top and stay hard inside.
Beat the eggs with the cottage cheese, sour cream, sugar, vanilla and salt, then fold in the noodles and raisins.
Pour into the dish, dot with the rest of the butter, dust with cinnamon and bake 45 minutes until set and golden. Good warm, better cold from the fridge the next morning.

name: Macaroni salad
steps: Cook the macaroni a minute past al dente, drain, and while it is still hot toss it with the vinegar and sugar. Hot pasta takes on the sour-sweet edge that keeps the whole bowl from tasting only of mayonnaise.
Let it cool, then fold in the mayonnaise and mustard.
Add the celery, onion, pickles and carrot.
Chill at least an hour — it is flat straight away and right after a rest.
Check the seasoning again cold, add the dill, and loosen with a spoonful of pickle brine if it has tightened.

name: Lemon, spinach and white bean orzo
steps: Fry the shallots in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes, until deep brown and crisp at the edges. Lift them onto paper and salt them.
Toast the orzo in the same pan for 2 minutes, then add the garlic for thirty seconds.
Add the stock a ladleful at a time, stirring, until the orzo is tender and the pan is creamy rather than soupy — about 10 minutes. Stirring is what releases the starch, and the starch is the sauce.
Stir in the beans, cream and spinach and cook until the spinach has collapsed.
Off the heat, add the lemon zest and juice, the parmesan and the pepper. Pile the crisp shallots over the top.

name: Roasted pepper and goat cheese rigatoni
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the peppers, onion and unpeeled garlic with the oil, thyme and salt and roast 25 minutes, until the edges are properly blackened in places.
Cook the pasta in well-salted water and keep a mugful of the water back.
Squeeze the garlic out of its skins and blitz it with half the peppers, the goat cheese and enough pasta water to make a loose sauce.
Toss the sauce through the pasta with the remaining peppers and onion, loosening with more water until it coats.
Finish with the chili flakes, basil and pepper.

name: Miso butter mushroom tagliatelle
steps: Mash the miso into the softened butter and set it aside.
Get a wide pan very hot with the vegetable oil. Add both mushrooms in one layer and leave them alone for 4 minutes so they brown instead of steaming.
Stir, cook 4 minutes more, then add the garlic for a final minute.
Cook the pasta and drag it straight into the pan with a ladle of its water. Add the miso butter and toss hard until it emulsifies into a glossy sauce.
Finish with the sesame oil, green onions and plenty of pepper. No cheese — the miso is already doing that job.

name: Charred broccoli orecchiette with pangrattato
steps: Toast the breadcrumbs in a third of the oil with one sliced garlic clove until deep gold. Tip them out — they will go soft if they sit in the pan.
Cook the pasta in well-salted water.
Meanwhile get the pan hot with the rest of the oil and char the broccoli hard, 6 minutes, turning it only twice. The black bits are the point.
Add the remaining garlic and the chili flakes for a minute, then the drained pasta and a splash of its water.
Toss with the pecorino, lemon zest and juice, and parsley. Scatter the pangrattato over at the table so it stays crisp.

name: Roasted squash, walnut and blue cheese pappardelle
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C and roast the squash in the oil with the salt for 25 minutes, until caramelised at the corners.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan and set aside. Fry the sage leaves in the butter until they stop sizzling, then lift them out.
Add the garlic to the sage butter for a minute, then the cream and two thirds of the squash. Crush the squash into the cream to thicken it.
Cook the pasta and toss it through with a splash of its water and most of the blue cheese.
Top with the remaining squash, the rest of the cheese, the walnuts, the crisp sage and plenty of pepper.

name: Charred zucchini, basil and pine nut farfalle
steps: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan and tip them out before they colour fully — they carry on cooking in their own heat.
Get the pan hot with half the oil and lay the zucchini in one layer. Leave it 4 minutes without touching it, then turn and give it 3 more. Crowding the pan steams it and you lose the dish.
Add the garlic and chili flakes for a minute and take the pan off the heat.
Cook the pasta and toss it in with a ladle of its water, the parmesan, the rest of the oil and the lemon zest and juice.
Tear the basil through at the last moment, season, and scatter the pine nuts over.

name: Harissa chickpea and lemon fusilli
steps: Fry the chickpeas in half the oil over high heat for 6 minutes, undisturbed at first, until some of them split and crisp.
Add the onion for 4 minutes, then the garlic, cumin and harissa for a minute more.
Cook the pasta and add it to the pan with a good ladle of its water, tossing until the harissa coats everything.
Take it off the heat before stirring in the yogurt, or it will split.
Finish with the lemon juice, parsley and the rest of the oil.

name: Creamy leek and pea linguine
steps: Wash the sliced leeks properly — grit hides between the layers and no amount of cream will hide it.
Sweat them in the butter and oil over low heat for 12 minutes with a pinch of salt, covered. They should collapse without colouring.
Add the garlic for a minute, then the cream and half the peas. Crush those peas roughly with a spoon to thicken the sauce.
Cook the pasta, adding the remaining peas for the last minute, and drag both into the pan with a ladle of the water.
Toss with the parmesan, lemon and mint, and season well.

name: Cauliflower and cashew korma
steps: Soak the cashews in boiling water for 15 minutes, then blend them with 250 ml of fresh water until completely smooth. Grittiness here never goes away later.
Start the rice. Brown the cauliflower in the oil over high heat in batches and set it aside.
Soften the onion in the same pan for 10 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and all the spices for a minute.
Pour in the cashew cream, return the cauliflower, and simmer covered for 12 minutes until tender.
Take the pan off the heat before stirring in the yogurt and salt, or it will split. Finish with cilantro and serve over the rice.

name: Tofu and green bean satay curry
steps: Start the rice. Press the tofu dry and brown it in the oil over high heat until crisp on several sides, then lift it out.
Soften the onion in the same pan for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and chili flakes.
Stir in the peanut butter and let it cook for a minute before adding the coconut milk — it seizes first and then loosens, which is what it is supposed to do.
Add the soy sauce, maple syrup and beans and simmer 8 minutes, until the sauce is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Return the tofu, warm through, and finish with lime juice, peanuts and cilantro.

name: Crispy halloumi and chickpea curry
steps: Fry the halloumi in half the oil until dark gold on every side and lift it out. Salt the pan lightly, not the cheese — halloumi brings its own.
Soften the onion in the rest of the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and spices for a minute.
Add the chickpeas and coconut milk and simmer 10 minutes, crushing a handful of the chickpeas to thicken it.
Fold the spinach through until it collapses, then the lemon juice and salt.
Return the halloumi at the very last moment so it keeps its crust, and serve with warm naan and cilantro.

name: Mushroom and lentil keema with peas
steps: Chop the mushrooms until they are the size of coarse mince. A food processor does it in seconds but will turn them to paste in ten, so pulse.
Brown them hard in the oil over high heat, 8 minutes, until the water has gone and they squeak in the pan.
Add the onion for 8 minutes, then the garlic, ginger and all the spices for a minute.
Add the lentils, stock and salt and simmer 25 minutes, until the lentils are soft and the pan is thick rather than wet. Stir in the peas for the last 3.
Serve with the roti, the yogurt spooned over and cilantro scattered on top.

name: Yellow split pea and squash curry
steps: Simmer the split peas in 1.2 litres of water with the turmeric for 30 minutes, until they collapse. They do not soften on any schedule but their own, so start them first.
Start the rice. Pop the mustard seeds in the oil over high heat — lid on, they jump — then add the onion for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin and curry powder for a minute, then the squash and a splash of water. Cover and cook 12 minutes.
Tip in the split peas with their liquid and the coconut milk and simmer 8 minutes, until it is thick enough to hold a line drawn across the pan.
Season, finish with lime juice and cilantro, and serve over the rice.

name: Paneer jalfrezi
steps: Fry the paneer in half the oil until gold on two sides and lift it out. It goes rubbery if it sits in the pan, so be quick about it.
Get the pan very hot with the rest of the oil and throw in the peppers and onion. Leave them almost alone for 5 minutes — this is a dry fry and they should blister, not stew.
Add the garlic, ginger and all the ground spices with the salt and toss for a minute.
Return the paneer with a bare splash of water, just enough to lift the spices off the pan, and toss until everything is coated.
Finish with lemon juice and cilantro and serve with naan. There is no sauce here by design — the char is the flavour.

name: Tempeh rendang
steps: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger and chilies into a rough paste with a splash of water.
Fry the tempeh in the oil until browned on both sides and set aside.
Fry the paste in the same pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, until it darkens and stops smelling raw. This is the step people cut short and it is the one that matters.
Add the spices, coconut milk, soy sauce, maple syrup and salt, return the tempeh, and simmer uncovered for 25 minutes.
Keep going until the sauce has reduced to a thick paste clinging to the tempeh and the oil comes back out. Finish with lime and serve with rice.

name: Black-eyed pea and kale curry
steps: Start the rice. Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder, allspice and thyme and cook 2 minutes, until the curry powder loses its dusty edge.
Add the coconut milk, the peas and the whole chili. Leaving it whole gives you its perfume without committing to its heat; burst it later if you want the heat.
Simmer 15 minutes, then fold the kale through in handfuls and cook 5 minutes more until it is tender.
Fish out the chili and thyme stalks, season, and finish with lime juice. Serve over the rice.

name: Caramelised onion and gruyère flatbread
steps: Cook the onions in the butter and one tablespoon of the oil over low heat for 30 minutes with a pinch of salt, stirring now and then. Rushing them on high heat gives you burnt onions, not sweet ones.
Heat the oven as high as it goes with a tray inside.
Stretch the dough thin and spread it with the sour cream, leaving a rim.
Scatter over the onions, the gruyère and the thyme leaves.
Bake 8-10 minutes on the hot tray until the edges are dark, and finish with pepper and the rest of the oil.

name: Harissa cauliflower flatbread with mint yogurt
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the cauliflower and chickpeas with two thirds of the harissa, the cumin, half the oil and the salt.
Roast 25 minutes on a hot tray, turning once, until the cauliflower is blackened at the tips and the chickpeas have tightened.
Stir the yogurt with the garlic, mint, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Warm the pitas in the oven for the last 2 minutes and brush them with the remaining harissa loosened with the rest of the oil.
Pile the cauliflower on, spoon the mint yogurt over, and scatter the raw onion on top for the bite.

name: Mushroom and taleggio flatbread
steps: Heat the oven as high as it will go with a tray inside.
Toss the mushrooms with half the oil and the salt and leave them 10 minutes, then squeeze them out hard. Raw mushrooms release their water onto the base and make it soggy.
Stretch the dough thin, scatter over the mushrooms, garlic and thyme, and dot the taleggio between them.
Bake 8-10 minutes on the hot tray, until the cheese has run and the edges are blistered.
Dress the arugula with the lemon and the rest of the oil and pile it on as it comes out of the oven.

name: Pesto, mozzarella and arugula flatbread
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C.
Spread the pitas with the pesto and top with the torn mozzarella and the pine nuts.
Bake 10 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and the edges have crisped.
Dress the arugula with the lemon juice and oil and pile it on straight away, so it wilts slightly rather than cooking.
Grind pepper over and cut into wedges.

name: Roasted grape and ricotta flatbread
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Roast the grapes with one tablespoon of the oil and the rosemary for 15 minutes, until some have burst and gone jammy.
Beat the ricotta with the salt and another tablespoon of oil until it is loose and spreadable.
Warm the pitas in the oven for 3 minutes, then spread them thickly with the ricotta.
Spoon the grapes and their syrupy juices over, and scatter the walnuts.
Finish with the honey, the last of the oil and a hard grind of pepper — it needs the pepper to stop being a dessert.

name: Spiced eggplant and labneh lavash
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the eggplant wedges with three quarters of the oil, the cumin and the salt — eggplant drinks oil, and underdoing it here gives you leather.
Roast 25 minutes, turning once, until collapsing and dark.
Stir the labneh with the garlic, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Warm the lavash in the oven for the last 2 minutes, then spread with the labneh and lay the eggplant over.
Scatter the za'atar, pomegranate and mint, and finish with the remaining oil.

name: Charred corn, chili and queso fresco flatbread
steps: Heat the oven as high as it goes with a tray inside.
Char the corn in a dry pan over the highest heat you have, 6 minutes, shaking it now and then. Dry pan, no oil — you want blackened kernels, not fried ones.
Toss the corn with the paprika, salt and half the oil.
Stretch the dough thin, scatter over the mozzarella, corn, onion and chili, and bake 8-10 minutes on the hot tray.
Crumble the queso fresco over as it comes out and finish with lime juice, cilantro and the rest of the oil.

name: Charred broccoli and pecorino flatbread
steps: Heat the oven as high as it will go with a tray inside.
Blanch the broccoli for 2 minutes, drain it very well, then toss with half the oil, the garlic, chili flakes and salt. Blanching first is what stops it going woody in the oven's short bake.
Stretch the dough thin and scatter over the mozzarella and broccoli.
Bake 8-10 minutes on the hot tray, until the florets have caught at their tips.
Grate the pecorino over while it is hot and finish with the lemon and the rest of the oil.
